START HERE: Google Ranker Pro / Hulk Marketing, 15 real-life videos

What this pack is. Everything you need to generate the raw footage for 15 short videos on Higgsfield, with copy-and-paste prompts in each video's file. Your job: generate clips with no text, captions, logos or graphics in them and send them back. Our job: the edit, which covers the real Search Console and Business Profile receipts, the before-and-after website comparisons, captions, disclosure labels, sound and both ratios.

Your brief, which every prompt follows: "It must not feel like AI, CGI, plastic or a 3D game render. It must look like a real-life shot."

2. MAKE TODAY (no one's photos needed)

Before the first generation, open Higgsfield and check three things. Is 1080p offered for Seedance 2.5? Is there a start-frame slot? Does a Soul ID appear as an Element? Tell us what you find.

Run these 15 generations first. They also test the realism. If a car looks like a game asset or a room looks rendered, we fix the World Bible blocks here, before anyone's face is involved.

3. THE PIPELINE in 7 steps

  1. Consent and photos. Get written consent covering likeness, voice, approved words, platforms, term and the right to withdraw. Then take 27 photos with the rear camera, window daylight, a plain wall and no filters or Portrait mode (research/production_rules.md A.2). Add 3 front-camera selfies for anyone in a selfie clip (V03, V07, V09, V12, V13's cold open, V14). Record voice memos: each approved line separately, 3 takes, 5–8 s, numbers said as words, quiet room, phone about 30 cm away (A.3). Send full-size files, never over WhatsApp. For premises, add 6–10 wide photos.
  2. Character sheet. Train a Soul ID on 20–30 photos and/or make a Nano Banana Pro sheet with the B.2 skeleton (3:2, 4k, count 4). Paste the person's wardrobe line verbatim (pack/characters/, or master_plan.md §3). No face description, ever. Build Hassan's sheet from fresh window-light photos, not his studio portraits.
  3. Crops. Cut the sheet into single views: front head, three-quarter left, three-quarter right, full body front, hands. Attach those, never the whole grid.
  4. Anchor still. Generate the anchor still first, then animate. Make one still per set-up with Soul 2.0 or Nano Banana Pro, at the deliverable ratio and in the capture mode's look. A shot needed in both ratios gets two stills. QC each still hard: skin pores, one light direction, no text, green screens showing all four corner dots.
  5. Seedance 2.5. Paste the prompt from the video file. Attach the @Image references in the order the ASSET MAP lists them. @Audio is used only for a real person's own memo, under 30 s in total.
  6. QC. Watch every clip at full resolution with sound before making the next. Use the checklist in production_rules.md §10. Change one thing per retry and log it. Never retry silently.
  7. Send back. See §7 below.

Higgsfield settings for every generation

  • Model Seedance 2.5 · Reference (omni-reference) mode · aspect ratio as the Gen ID says (16x9 / 9x16)
  • 1080p, set explicitly every time. It silently defaults lower. If only 720p is offered, use 720p and tell us; we upscale once in finishing.
  • Whole-second duration from the shot list · Audio on
  • Selectors: Era 2020s · Physics realistic · Tone calm or warm · Genre unset or documentary · Lens 24 mm for phone shots, 50 mm (or 85 mm for close-ups) for documentary-camera shots
  • If a selector is set, the prompt never repeats it. Never type a resolution into the prompt.

4. REALISM RULES IN ONE BOX

The 10 rules that make it look like real footage

  1. One named light source with falloff, pasted verbatim (window, lamp, street lamp, overcast sky). Name where the shadow falls. No golden hour, no sun, no studio or ring light.
  2. One capture mode per video (DOC-CAM, PHONE-SELFIE or PHONE-REAR). Its texture line goes last, verbatim. Never mix two modes in one clip.
  3. Atmosphere between lens and subject: rain on glass, breath in cold air, steam from a mug, drizzle, a smeared windscreen.
  4. Lived-in dressing: two or three anchors that stay put, plus one uncomposed element (a crooked blind, a cable on the floor, a half-cropped passer-by, a ticket face-down on the dash).
  5. Real physics and weight: chairs creak, sleeves drag, tea shivers, suspension settles. Every car gets the VEHICLE lock.
  6. Behaviour, not emotion: blinks, glances away, restarts a gesture, rubs the neck, a small nod. Never "looks happy" or "confident".
  7. The skin line: real people get Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.; anonymous hands get pores, fine hairs and one imperfection.
  8. Optics match the device: phones have deep focus and no creamy bokeh; DOC-CAM has a gently soft background. The camera behaves like a hand, a shoulder or a tripod, with no gimbal, drone, dolly or slow motion.
  9. Strip the hype: no cinematic, 8K, ultra-realistic, photorealistic, masterpiece, stunning, flawless, perfect, polished, professional, studio or glossy. No lens brands or ISO. No "no AI look"-style negations.
  10. One wet week in October: paste the palette line for the scene (exterior, interior or car), keep colours muted, add no readable text anywhere, and make every screen turned away, soft or flat green with four corner dots.

If a clip looks like AI, CGI, plastic or a game render: fix in this order, one change per retry

  • Plastic or waxy skin: strip any hype words → check the person has no face prose → check whether the anchor still was glossy and remake it → only then add natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, no smoothing.
  • Game render (even light, everything sharp, too clean): name one light source with falloff → add two dressing anchors and one uncomposed element → add atmosphere → add physics lines → as a last resort, put No game-engine look, no CG gloss. next to the light line.
  • Toy-like car: VEHICLE lock → a real car photo as a prop reference → a shorter shot with the camera static while the car moves.
  • Floaty motion: add physics lines, use one action per stage and make the clip shorter. Gimbal-smooth camera: paste the handheld line and remove the move words.
  • Full table: production_rules.md D.7.

5. HONESTY IN ONE BOX

  • Real people come only from their own photos, with written consent. A generated face attached to a real name or a real quote is a fabricated testimonial, which the DMCC Act 2024 and the CAP Code ban. A face and a voice are also personal data. So: no consent, no clip. Never describe a real person's face, and never generate an "Ali".
  • Client words: we send questions, not sentences. The client answers in a voice memo, we transcribe it, they approve it, and only then do their exact words go into the prompt. Until then the prompt shows [APPROVED LINE n FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]. Owners say no numbers; the numbers are ours, on screen with a source. Agency people edit and approve our drafts.
  • Disclosure labels (on screen throughout; you and your adviser confirm the final wording):
    • Real person, re-created: AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data.
    • Real voice over faceless footage: Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.
    • AI presenter (fallback only): AI presenter. Real client data. Not a client testimonial.
    • No-face b-roll: Illustrative footage. Real data. (V04: Dramatised reconstruction · Real data)
  • Platform labels on every post: TikTok AI-generated content (AIGC) toggle, YouTube "altered or synthetic content", Meta "AI info".
  • No "No.1", "#1", "first", "just hit", "now", growth figures or up-arrows until there is a dated ranking capture or a Search Console Compare export. 1.8 is said as "top two on average".
  • Every number comes from assets/gsc/gsc_data.json or a dated capture of a live site. Impressions are "times shown", never "people".
  • This matches what your site already does: googlerankerpro.com labels its presenters "AI-generated presenters and voices. Service explanations, not client testimonials."

6. WHAT WE STILL NEED FROM YOU (most blocking first)

  • Consent, 27 photos and voice memos from each person on camera or voice: Golden Line owner, Coventry owner, Leam Taxis owner, York Cars manager, Organic Fostering director, Hassan, T1, T2 (and Sajid if wanted). Who are T1 (SEO specialist) and T2 (reporting lead)?
  • Which business owns each Business Profile screenshot: is the 114-calls profile Leam Taxis', and is the 79-interactions profile Coventry Airport Taxis 247's? Please also send Coventry's Calls tab and per-type breakdown. (Blocks V03, V04, V09, V12, T2's number in V10 and the V13 montage.)
  • Agency credit and permission to name, per client: Coventry's footer says SMEK; York Cars' says Xoom Media; Leam Taxis appears only in Hulk's portfolio; who built Organic Fostering's Sept 2026 rebuild; Hulk's role on Zentro.
  • Work logs: Golden Line (for V01, T1's task in V10 and V15); Coventry if its June 2026 pages should become a later episode.
  • T2's real location (UK or Pakistan) and photos of the real workplace(s). Does T2 really send Leam Taxis' report? (Blocks V12.)
  • Photos of your real agency room and desk (for V08, V10, V11, V13, V14, V15).
  • York Cars' own yard and dispatch-office photos, and which address is the dispatch office. (No V05 without them.)
  • Search Console Compare exports (previous 3 months or 16 months) for Golden Line and Coventry. Without them we never say growth, "just hit" or "now".
  • Dated ranking proof (a query report or SERP capture) for any "No.1" claim.
  • Real phone footage, RF01–RF08: 8–10 s overcast clips of Warwick (Castle Bridge, Market Place), Leamington (The Parade), Kenilworth, York (Station, Minster), the Coventry ring road, Chester Road in Old Trafford with a bus, one dashcam drive per town, and permission to reuse Organic Fostering's 19 Drive clips.
  • Wayback "before" captures from your own browser: the archive refused our connection. Needed: yorkcars.co.uk snapshot 20250916232610 and Coventry before June 2026. Steps are in research/wayback_before.md.
  • Higgsfield UI check: is 1080p offered for Seedance 2.5, is there a start-frame slot, and does a Soul ID appear as an Element?
  • Also: are Leam Taxis, Golden Line and Coventry one operator group? Which brand appears on screen per placement (GRP, Hulk, or "Hulk Marketing · part of Google Ranker Pro")? Site fixes are needed before captures (Coventry's Slough review widget and typos; Golden Line's test pages). We need sign-off on the label wording, and permission for the tip episodes (York Cars fares, Zentro).

7. HOW TO SEND CLIPS BACK

  • File name: grp_vNN_<setup>-<shot>_t<take>_<ratio>.mp4, for example grp_v04_P-01_t2_9x16.mp4 or grp_v01_A-03_t1_16x9.mp4. For the b-roll bank, use grp_BR01_t1_16x9.mp4. V10 adds the person before the shot: grp_v10_T1_A-01_t1_16x9.mp4.
  • Variants keep the same pattern, with a letter added to the shot: C for an anonymous (Mode C) twin (grp_v09_B-01C_t1_9x16.mp4), RF for real footage you film yourself in place of a generated shot (grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4), x for an extension (grp_v02_A-01x_t1_16x9.mp4), and a / b for a shot split in two (grp_v12_A-02a_t1_9x16.mp4). New real-footage shots with no generated twin use RF as the set-up (grp_v13_RF-01_t1_16x9.mov). Clips for the shared real-footage list in §6 (RF01–RF08) are named RF<nn>_<place>_<n>, for example RF03_kenilworth_1.mov. Clips you film keep your phone's own file type (.mov or .mp4).
  • Download at the generated resolution (MOV where offered).
  • Send the passing takes and the near-misses. A good first half is still usable.
  • Send the anchor stills and the character-sheet crops as well.
  • Add a short note giving the resolution used (1080p or 720p) and the selectors you set.

What we do in the edit: we add the real Search Console and Business Profile receipts (exact crops with source and date) and key them into every green screen. We build the before-and-after website comparisons from real captures only, and add word-timed captions inside the safe zones and the disclosure labels. We lay in the real voice memos and ambience and mix to −14 LUFS for social. Each video is cut in both ratios where the plan calls for it, with one light grade and one upscale route per video.

2. Consent: get these in writing before any photo is used

Sign this even though he is a director of the company. The signed form is the record behind the disclosure label and the platform AI-content toggles.

  • Voice: his own voice memos are used as the @Audio reference in Seedance and laid in as the final soundtrack. If a lip-sync repair is needed, it uses his real memo. We do not clone or synthesise his voice for new words.
  • Approved words only: he edits and approves every line in writing before recording, and approves the final cut before it is published. Nothing he has not said and heard goes out.

  • Term and storage: a fixed term (the user sets it, e.g. 24 months, renewable). His photos, Soul ID, sheets and memos are personal data, stored privately and deleted at the end of the term or on request.
  • Withdrawal: he can withdraw at any time. We take the videos down from our own pages and accounts within an agreed number of days and delete the Soul ID, sheets and memos. Copies that others have already shared cannot be recalled, and the form says so.

3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

Set-up (2 min)

  • Someone else holds the phone. Use the rear main camera and wipe the lens first. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all off.
  • Stand facing a big window at about 45° on an overcast day, in front of a plain mid-tone wall (not white, not green, no posters, nobody else in frame).
  • Head-and-shoulders photos at 2x zoom from about 1.5 m. Full-body photos at 1x from about 3 m.
  • Avoid: sunglasses, hats, harsh direct sun, office strip lights on their own, ring lights, coloured LEDs, edits. Use today's haircut and beard. Glasses only if he always wears them, and then in every photo.

Round 1: DESK outfit, all 27 photos (8 min) (plain navy crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt, dark trousers, his own watch)

5. Soul ID training note

  • Train a Soul for Hassan: yes. He appears in many solo shots (23 generations), which is exactly the case a Soul is for. Ask him first, and train only after the consent form is signed.
  • Training set: 25 photos, all from this shoot: 15 DESK (#1–20, minus the full-body back and profiles if you are short), 7 SUIT, and the 3 DESK selfies. Leave out hands, the collar close-up and location photos, because they carry no face.
  • Where it works: a Soul runs only on soul_2 and soul_cinematic, one Soul per generation. Anchor stills: Nano Banana Pro from the crops plus the real place photos (the video file's Step 1). Use a soul_2 still only after two logged identity-drift retries, and attach the place photo if the Soul 2.0 screen accepts one. Check in the UI whether the Soul also appears as an Element for Seedance. If it does not, use the sheet crops below as @Image references.
  • Sheet instead of Soul: for any frame with a second identity (the optional V13 two-shot with Sajid), and whenever the Soul drifts. In a two-person shot, make each sheet's front and three-quarter crops into Reference Elements and build the anchor still on nano_banana_pro. Never more than two identities in one generation.
  • If the Soul and the sheet disagree on his likeness, his real photos decide. Log which one passed.

7. Voice memos

How to record

  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen). Hold the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly off to one side.
  • Use the Voice Memos app on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder. Mono, one voice, no music or TV. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take clips, record it again.
  • Make one file per line, with three takes inside it and a 2-second gap between takes. Each take is 5–8 s, said the way he would say it on the phone to a client, not read out.
  • Numbers are spoken as words, exactly as written. His accent is never described anywhere in text. The existing founder clips are silent, so every memo is new.
  • File name: MEMO_F1_HASSAN_<video>_line<n>.m4a, for example MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v14_line3.m4a.

What to record. These are agency drafts. Hassan edits them and approves them in writing before recording. Lines marked G7 are recorded only once the Golden Line work log confirms them.

Rules for the lines.

  • Every number above matches gsc_data.json:
    • taxi warwick: 665 times shown, average position 10.7, 0.9% click-through.

    • kenilworth taxis: 6.7.
    • 665 + 486 + 371 = 1,522, at averages 10.7 to 12.6.
  • If he rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.
  • Never "last quarter", "people saw", "No.1", "first", or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
  • If the generated voice does not sound like him, it fails QC. Fix it in the order set out in production_rules G.1.

7. Voice memos

How to record (production_rules A.3):

  • Room: a quiet room with soft furnishings, not a kitchen or stairwell. No music, no TV.
  • Phone: about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly off to one side. Mono. Lossless setting, or 44.1/48 kHz.
  • Takes and level: record each line separately, three takes per line, with peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. Re-record any take that clips.
  • Delivery: say it as you would on the phone to a client, not as if reading.
  • Numbers: say them as words, exactly as written. They must match the receipt.

File names

  • Takes: MEMO_T1_SEO_<video>_line<n>_t1.m4a, _t2, _t3.
  • We keep the best take as MEMO_T1_SEO_<video>_line<n>.m4a.
  • Send the files full size, never over WhatsApp.

3. Photo shoot (20 minutes on a phone, at their real desk)

Set-up (2 minutes)

  • Camera: someone else takes the photos with the rear main camera. Wipe the lens. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all off.
  • Distance: heads at 2× from about 1.5 m; full body at 1× from about 3 m.
  • Light: window daylight at about 45°, or open shade. If T2 is in Pakistan, never shoot in direct sun. Shoot indoors by a window, in open shade, or in the early morning, because harsh sun ruins both skin texture and the Soul.
  • Background: a plain mid-tone wall, not white and not green, with no posters, no text and nobody else in frame.
  • Look as on the day of filming: the same hair and glasses (wear them in every photo if they always do). No sunglasses and no heavy makeup.
  • Headscarf, hijab or dupatta: if T2 wears one, they wear it exactly as they will in the videos, in every photo. It is part of their wardrobe, and the rule against "scarves over the face" does not apply to it.

Their own style first. The plan's line is a navy knit jumper with the sleeves pushed up. If that is not what T2 really wears to work (a jumper in a warm Lahore October, for example, or sleeves they would not push up), photograph what they really wear: plain, mid-tone, no logos, no green and no fine stripes. Then rewrite the wardrobe line once, in step 4 and step 8, and use the new line everywhere.

7. Voice memos

How to record (production_rules A.3):

  • Room: a quiet room with soft furnishings. No fan, no TV. In Pakistan, turn the ceiling fan off while recording.
  • Phone: about 30 cm from the mouth. Mono. Lossless setting, or 44.1/48 kHz.
  • Takes and level: each line separately, three takes, peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. Re-record anything that clips.
  • Delivery: speak as you would on the phone to a client.
  • Accent: use their own natural accent. It is never described in text and never changed.

3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

Set-up (2 min)

  • Someone else holds the phone. Use the rear main camera and wipe the lens. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all off.
  • Light: face a large window at about 45°, or stand outdoors in open shade on an overcast day. Use a plain mid-tone wall behind him (not white, not green), with no posters, signs or other people.
  • Head-and-shoulders photos at 2x zoom from about 1.5 m. Full-body photos at 1x from about 3 m.
  • Wear: his own dark quilted jacket over a plain grey fleece, the exact pieces he will "wear" in V01. If his jacket carries a company logo or hi-vis lettering, use a plain one instead and tell us which.
  • Avoid: sunglasses, caps or beanies, a hi-vis vest, harsh direct sun, strip lights on their own, any edits. Use today's hair and beard. Glasses only if he always wears them, and then in every photo.

7. Voice memos

How to record

  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen). Hold the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side. No TV, no radio, no dispatch chatter.
  • Use the Voice Memos app on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder. Mono, one voice. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take clips, record it again.
  • Step 1, the interview: one relaxed memo of 5 to 10 minutes answering our four questions, said the way he'd tell another driver:
    • Q1 "Before you worked with Hulk, where did your bookings come from, and what was missing?"
    • Q2 "What changed when the new site went live?"
    • Q3 "What's different now, day to day?"
    • Q4 "If another taxi firm asked you about it, what would you tell them?"
    • Q5 (only if the V03 fallback runs): "What are the Kenilworth jobs like for you?"
  • Step 2: we transcribe it and send him the lines. He approves them in writing.
  • Step 3: he records each approved line as its own file, with three takes and a 2-second gap between takes. Each take lasts 5 to 8 s.
  • His accent is never described anywhere in text.
  • File name: MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_<video>_line<n>.m4a.

9. Sheet QC: five checks before cropping

Log each attempt as QC [date] CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER sheet_jacket t[n] [nano_banana_pro] / Verdict PASS|FAIL / Failure: symptom > broken lock > fix. Change one thing per retry.

# Check If it fails, first fix (production_rules D.7)
1 Resemblance: put the front and both three-quarter panels beside his real photos #1, #5 and #6. Someone who knows him should say "that's him" at a glance. Identity drift: use fewer words about the person (confirm no face prose has crept in), attach the identity photos first and include a three-quarter photo. Then try a soul_2 still.
2 Skin not smoothed: at 100% zoom you can see pores and real texture, with no wax or airbrushing, and he is not de-aged or made to look rested. Plastic skin: strip any hype words and confirm Mode B. Check the source photos were not taken in beauty or Portrait mode, and reshoot them if they were.
3 No text or logos on the jacket or fleece, no hi-vis lettering, and no labels or numbers in the gutters. Gibberish text: name the clothes as plain (the wardrobe line already does), then fix the area with a region edit.
4 Consistent light: the same soft overhead camera-left light on mid-grey in all twelve panels, with no dark studio look and no hard side light. Looks like a render: name the one real light source with falloff, and check that no website image was attached.
5 Hands: five fingers on each hand, natural knuckle creases, working hands that are not manicured-looking. D.7 has no hands row. Add the HANDS lock (Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.), or pick a different one of the 4 variants.

Character sheets: York Cars and Organic Fostering (CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER, CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR)

These are two real clients, each filmed in their own real workplace: the York Cars manager in the yard and dispatch office (V05), and the Organic Fostering director or registered manager at the office table in Beaumont House (V06). Neither business names anyone publicly, so you ask each client who will appear and how they want to be captioned. Both are Mode B. The face comes only from their own photos, used with written consent. The words are their own answers, transcribed by us and approved by them. The voice is their own voice memo. No prompt ever describes their face. Every shot puts the person inside a real place, so the location also comes only from the client's own photos: no York Cars photos means no V05, and no Beaumont House photos means V06 runs as the text-only fallback. Work through each person in order: consent, photos, sheet, crops, voice.

Before you start, for both people

  • Settings for every sheet: Nano Banana Pro (nano_banana_pro) · 3:2 · 4k · count 4, pick the best of the four. On the Higgsfield MCP, load the character-sheet workflow first.
  • What a sheet prompt contains: the B.2 layout, the wardrobe line copied exactly, one skin line and one imperfection. It contains no description of the face, hair, skin tone, age or build.
  • On-screen label (we add it in the edit): AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Their words, their voice. Real data. If the client prefers a role to a name, use the role, e.g. "the operations manager at York Cars".
  • Client words stay as [APPROVED LINE n FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] until the client approves them in writing. They quote no numbers. All numbers appear on screen in the edit, with their source.

CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER · York Cars owner or operations manager (real client, name to be confirmed) · Mode B

The owner or operations manager of York Cars, a licensed private-hire firm in York. Nobody is named on yorkcars.co.uk, so the client tells you who appears and how they are captioned. On screen they have night-shift energy: a radio earpiece, a lanyard turned round, keys in hand, a jacket damp from the drizzle. They walk us from the wet yard, through the door, into the dispatch room.

3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone)

Set-up (2 min)

  • Someone else holds the phone. Use the rear main camera and wipe the lens. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all off.
  • Shoot in daylight, even though V05 is a night film. Use a window at about 45° on an overcast day, or open shade in the yard. Do not shoot at night under the yard lamps or under the office strip lights on their own.
  • Use a plain mid-tone wall behind them: not white, not green, no posters, no signage, nobody else in frame.
  • Head-and-shoulders photos at 2x zoom from about 1.5 m. Full body at 1x from about 3 m.
  • Wear the WORK outfit: their own dark work jacket over a plain sweatshirt. If the jacket has a York Cars logo or name on it, cover it with matching tape or wear a plain one, because the wardrobe line says "no company lettering". The same goes for a hi-vis vest: plain, or the lettering taped over.
  • Take the lanyard and radio earpiece off for photos #1–20, so the sheet stays clean. They come back in the prop photos below.
  • Avoid: sunglasses, hats, harsh sun, ring lights, coloured LEDs, edits, and any photo older than about 4 months. Use today's hair and beard. Glasses only if they always wear them, and then in every photo.

The 27 photos, WORK outfit (10 min)

# Shot
1–4 Head and shoulders, front: neutral, soft natural smile, mid-word as if talking, real laugh
5–8 Three-quarter left, three-quarter right, profile left, profile right (all neutral)
9–12 Chin slightly up, chin slightly down, looking off camera left, looking off camera right
13–17 Waist up: front, three-quarter left, three-quarter right; glancing back over the shoulder as if leading someone across the yard (V05 W-01); talking with one hand mid-gesture
18–20 Full body: front, back (the walk shots are mostly from behind), three-quarter
21–22 Hands, backs and palms; holding their real keys the way they always do
23 Close-up of the jacket collar, zip and sweatshirt neckline
24–26 Skip. They have no selfie shots.
27 Standing by the real office door in the yard, in daylight

Prop photos (2 min): the radio earpiece in their ear (note which ear), the lanyard worn with the card turned to face the body (note: card never shown front-on), the keys on their fob or carabiner, and the hi-vis vest if they really wear one in the yard.

Location photos (6 min; anyone at York Cars can take these): 6–10 wide photos of each place, from the corners at standing eye height, lights as normal.

  • The yard (L5): in daylight, plus 2–3 at night with the yard lamps on, from where the camera will walk, so we know where the lamp really is. Include the walk from the parked cars to the office door, and the door itself.
  • The dispatch office (L5): radios on chargers, keys on hooks, the kettle, a coat on a chair. Turn every monitor off or away before you shoot, because dispatch screens show customer addresses and phone numbers. No rota boards or whiteboards with names in frame.

2. Consent: get each point in writing, signed before the photos are used

  • Likeness and AI re-creation: we may make a Nano Banana Pro character sheet (and a Soul ID only if they tick that box) from their photos, and generate the five listed V06 shots of them and nothing else without asking again.   • The organisation: Organic Fostering Ltd agrees, as a regulated agency, to its office being photographed and re-created, to being named, and to Hulk being named as the agency it worked with. The office photos show no carers, no children, no case files and no names.

  • Term and storage: a fixed term (the user sets it, e.g. 24 months, renewable). Photos, sheet, any Soul and the memos are personal data, stored privately and deleted at the end of the term or on request.

3. Photo shoot checklist (about 20 minutes on a phone, in the office)

Set-up (2 min)

  • A colleague holds the phone. Use the rear main camera and wipe the lens. Portrait mode, beauty mode, filters and flash all off.
  • Stand facing the office window at about 45° on an overcast day, in front of a plain mid-tone wall (not white, not green, no notices, nobody else in frame). Do not rely on the ceiling lights alone.
  • Head-and-shoulders photos at 2x zoom from about 1.5 m. Full body at 1x from about 3 m.
  • Wear the CARDIGAN outfit: a soft grey knit cardigan over a plain top, with the lanyard on and the card turned to face the body. Plain, mid-tone, no logos, no fine stripes, no green. If they never wear a grey cardigan, photograph what they really wear in the same spirit and tell us, so we rewrite the wardrobe line once.
  • Avoid: sunglasses, harsh sun, ring lights, coloured LEDs, heavy makeup, edits, and any photo older than about 4 months. Today's hair. Glasses only if they always wear them, and then in every photo.

The 27 photos, CARDIGAN outfit (10 min)

# Shot
1–4 Head and shoulders, front: neutral, soft natural smile, mid-word as if talking, real laugh
5–8 Three-quarter left, three-quarter right, profile left, profile right (all neutral)
9–12 Chin slightly up, chin slightly down, looking off camera left, looking off camera right
13–17 Waist up: front, three-quarter left, three-quarter right; seated at the real office table with a mug of tea, eyes just past the camera to its left (V06 A-01); talking with one hand mid-gesture
18–20 Full body: front, back, three-quarter
21–22 Hands, backs and palms; holding their own mug, and writing with a pen on a blank notebook page (V06 B-01)
23 Close-up of the cardigan's knit, buttons and the neckline of the top
24–26 Skip. They have no selfie shots.
27 Seated at the real office table by the window, as they will be filmed

Prop photos (1 min): their own mug (plain, no print; tell us if it has one), the plain notebook and pen, the plant on the table, and any watch or ring they always wear (note which hand).

Location photos (7 min): 6–10 wide photos of the office at Beaumont House, from the corners at standing eye height, lights as normal, on an overcast day.

  • Include the table, the window behind it onto Chester Road (a bus passing is a bonus), the plant, and the chair they sit in.
  • Before you shoot, clear the room: no case files, no children's photos or drawings, no whiteboards or wall planners with names, no carers' details, no Ofsted certificate or logo boards in frame. Turn every screen off or away.
  • If you can, add one 8–10 s phone clip of Chester Road from the window with a bus passing in drizzle (RF06).
  • No children anywhere in frame, including on the pavement or in the bus windows; if one appears, retake or discard the clip.

Send: original full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email at actual size. Never WhatsApp. Name the photos CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_01.jpg to _27.jpg, and the folders PHOTOS_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_cardigan, PHOTOS_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_props and PHOTOS_L6_beaumont_house.

This file covers the two cast members who are not real, named people. N1 is an invented woman: a clearly labelled AI presenter. Prompt 1: the character sheet (Mode A, human-realism 13 blocks). Settings: Nano Banana Pro · 3:2 · 4k · count 4. No attachments. Tightened from master_plan §3.2. The far side of her face gets the light's falloff on three features. Her brows have a few stray hairs but no grey, because the age ladder puts sparse, greying brows at about 65, not 55.

Image prompt · 2,941 characters
Character reference sheet of one invented woman, photographed as twelve equal panels in a 4 by 3 grid with thin plain mid-grey gutters and no labels, no text, no numbers. Row one, head and shoulders at eye level: front facing with a calm neutral expression; three-quarter view turned to her left; three-quarter view turned to her right; left profile. Row two: full body front, head to feet; full body from behind; full body three-quarter view; both hands held up, backs in one and palms in the other. Row three, head and shoulders: a relaxed half-smile; mid-word as if talking, lips slightly parted; thinking, eyes looking just off camera to the left; close-up of the collar and knit of her cardigan. Around 55 years old, a practical woman who has run a busy office most of her working life, but clearly someone who still laughs easily at the end of a long day. White British, fair, warm-toned skin with redness around the nostrils, grey-green eyes, natural brows with a few stray hairs. Chin-length ash-brown hair with grey coming through at the parting, tucked behind one ear, flyaways at the crown and a cowlick at the front hairline. A small pale scar through her left eyebrow. Thin tortoiseshell reading glasses pushed up into her hair. Maximum realism (skin AND hair): moderate wrinkles, horizontal forehead lines, crow's feet, deepening nasolabial folds, faint under-eye hollows with darker circles, early vertical lip lines, a slightly softened jawline, visible pores, uneven pigmentation and mild darker patches, a few sun spots, a small dry patch beside one nostril, peach fuzz along the jaw and upper lip. Do not smooth, soften, rejuvenate or beautify her skin. Detailed grey-green irises with visible fibre texture, natural moisture, tiny visible vessels in the sclera, authentic catchlights. Individual hair strands, eyebrow hairs and eyelashes sharply visible. Her hair looks genuinely grown from the scalp, never painted or artificially perfect. The scar has realistic healed tissue texture and slight tonal variation. Her hands show natural knuckle creases, faint veins and short plain nails, five fingers on each hand. She carries herself plainly and without fuss. No obvious makeup. Wearing a moss-green wool cardigan over a cream crew-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, reading glasses pushed up into her hair; no logos, no printed text, in every panel. The cardigan is a little bobbled at the cuffs; plain flat dark shoes, scuffed at the toes. Seamless neutral mid-grey background (#8C8C8C) in every panel. One large soft light overhead and slightly to camera-left with even soft fill, gentle natural shadow under the chin and nose, the same light in every panel; the far side of her face falls a little darker, with soft shadow in the nasolabial fold, under the cheekbone and beneath the brow. Head panels framed like an 85mm portrait lens, body panels like a 50mm lens, no wide-angle distortion. Fine natural photographic grain.

The words "artificially perfect" are part of human-realism's fixed hair sentence (block 11), which tells the model what to avoid. They are not a hype token, so leave them in.

If it comes back glossy or waxy, remove the sentence "Do not smooth, soften, rejuvenate or beautify her skin." first (on Nano Banana Pro it can read as noise), then regenerate. Never add hype words to fix it.

6. Crops

None. Extras have no sheet, so there are no CROP_EXTRA_MODE_C_* files. Attach these instead:

7. Voice

None. Extras never speak intelligibly. They record no memos and have no synthetic voice. Ambience and foley come from their actions: the finger taps on the wheel, the boot thunk, the trolley rattle, the chair creak, the radio crackle. Use the audio lock in step 4.

What this video is

  • Concept. A Warwick taxi owner, parked up before sunrise, tells us in his own words what it was like when Google sent no work his way, what changed when the new site went live, and what's different now. Problem (his own car, pre-dawn) → turn (his own back office at dusk, laptop open with a green screen) → result (the real Search Console receipts).
  • Hook. Black. A wiper thunks once. A phone lights up face-up on a dark dashboard and buzzes against the plastic. Over it, the first sentence of his real answer. No title for 6 s. (9:16: the same image with 312 clicks · 18.2K times shown on screen by 0.8 s.)
  • Why this brand. Golden Line is the only client with a verified Hulk credit on its live site (footer: "Made with ❤ by Hulk Marketing Ltd") and an attributed Search Console screenshot.
  • What the edit reveals. At ~37 s the live footer credit is pushed in as proof of the work. At 49 s (65% of the runtime) the real totals land on his laptop's green screen and push to full frame: 312 clicks, 18.2K times shown, 744 different searches, brand searches top two on average (1.8), two airport searches on page one on average. He says no numbers. The numbers are ours, on screen, sourced and dated.
  • The motif. The film opens and closes on a phone lighting up, its screen never readable.

Script and voice memos

DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. We send him questions, not sentences. He answers in one relaxed memo, we transcribe it, he approves the exact lines in writing, then he records each approved line on its own. Every [APPROVED LINE n FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT] in the prompts is replaced with his exact approved words, nothing else.

The four questions (send these as they are):

  1. "Before you worked with Hulk, where did your bookings come from, and what was missing?"
  2. "What changed when the new site went live? Say it the way you'd tell another driver."
  3. "What's different now, day to day?"
  4. "If another taxi firm asked you about it, what would you tell them?"

Ask him: no numbers, no "number one", "No.1", "first" or "just hit", no "now" as a before-and-after claim, no review wording, no "Ali". The numbers are ours, on screen.

Picking lines 6, 6b and 7: skip any sentence that claims more work, more calls or a before-and-after change ("more", "busier", "up", "doubled") unless he can show his own booking records (G5).

How he records a memo (send him this):

  • First, one relaxed interview memo of 5–10 minutes answering the four questions: MEMO_CLIENT_GOLDENLINE_OWNER_v01_interview.m4a.
  • After approval, one approved line per memo, three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take must fit its slot: lines 1, 3, 4 and 6 at most 6 s; lines 2, 5 and 7 at most 5 s (line 6b is voice only and can run to 6 s; line 0 is cut from the interview memo). Time each trimmed memo before attaching it. If one runs long, ask for a shorter take; don't stretch the prompt.
  • A quiet room with soft furnishings (lounge or bedroom, not the kitchen, not the car with the engine on). No TV, radio or dispatch chatter.
  • Phone about 30 cm from his mouth, slightly to one side (stops pops).
  • Voice Memos app on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way he'd say it to a customer on the phone, not read out.
  • Send the files full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • His accent is never described anywhere. His memo carries his voice.

If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, it fails QC. We lay his real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1).

Image prompt · 1,868 characters
A low view across the dark dashboard of a parked car before dawn in late October, the camera resting on the passenger side of the dashboard and looking diagonally across towards the driver's door, so the rain-speckled windscreen fills the upper half of the frame and the driver's seat sits just out of frame to the right. A smartphone in a plain dark case lies face-up on the flat top of the dashboard about 60 centimetres from the lens, its screen dark and seen edge-on, so only its thin side and the edge of the case show. The wiper has stopped part-way up the glass, leaving a smeared arc in the rain; the bottom edge of the windscreen is misted. Outside, a wet terraced street, soft and grey, one amber street lamp blurred into a soft ball of light. A parking ticket lies face-down at the far end of the dashboard; a charging cable lies coiled at the near end of the dashboard, soft; fine dust and a thumb smear on the dashboard plastic. Nobody in frame. About 47° field of view, the street outside softly out of focus. Blue-grey early daylight through the car windows mixed with the warm amber of street lamps outside; the dashboard stays dark; rain beads on the glass catch small points of light. Muted colour inside a parked car as it really looks: a charcoal dashboard and grey seat fabric, rain beads on the glass, the world outside soft and grey; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. No people in frame. Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.
  • Step 2 · Seedance 2.5 prompt:
Seedance 2.5 prompt · 5,100 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light, dashboard layout, the phone's position and the stopped wiper in frame one; frame one matches it exactly; do not copy any text.

SCENE CONTEXT
Before dawn in late October, a phone lying face-up on the dark dashboard of a parked car lights up and buzzes against the plastic, and a driver's hand reaches across from the driver's seat and lifts it away.

LOCATION MAP
Camera resting on the passenger side of the dashboard at dashboard height, facing diagonally across towards the driver's door; the driver's seat is just out of frame to the right. Foreground: dark dashboard plastic with fine dust and a thumb smear, soft. Midground: the phone in a plain dark case, lying face-up on the flat top of the dashboard 60 centimetres from the lens, its screen edge-on to the lens. Background: the windscreen with rain beads and a smeared arc where the wiper stopped part-way up the glass, its lower edge misted, and a wet terraced street outside, soft and grey, with one amber street lamp blurred. A parking ticket face-down at the far end of the dashboard; a charging cable lying coiled at the near end of the dashboard, soft.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already shows the phone dark and still on the dashboard, its screen facing straight up at the roof and seen only edge-on, the wiper stopped part-way up the windscreen, rain on the glass. No hand in frame yet.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE. Camera static.

OPTICS
47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera about 60 centimetres from the phone, natural perspective, zero obvious distortion, the street outside readable but softly out of focus.

CAMERA
Static, resting on the dashboard; only a faint tremor runs through the frame when the hand touches the dashboard at second 4. Focus stays on the phone.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The phone lies dark and still; rain beads sit on the windscreen. End state: unchanged frame.
1-4s: At second 1 the phone lights; its cool glow spreads across the roof lining and the inside of the windscreen. It buzzes against the dashboard in two short pulses and creeps a few millimetres sideways on the plastic. End state: phone lit and still on the dashboard.
4-5s: At second 4 a driver's left hand enters from frame right, the fingers close around the edges of the case and lift the phone off the dashboard, its screen tilting towards the driver and away from the lens. End state: hand and phone leaving the right edge of frame.
5-6s: The dashboard is empty where the phone lay; the glow has gone with it; rain on the glass. Ambience only. End state: empty dashboard, camera holding.

PHYSICS
The phone has weight: each buzz rattles it against the hard plastic and it shifts a few millimetres; the fingertips press into the case as they grip; the dashboard flexes very slightly under the hand; rain beads gather and slide slowly down the windscreen; the car does not move.

LIGHTING
Blue-grey early daylight through the car windows mixed with the warm amber of street lamps outside; the dashboard stays dark; rain beads on the glass catch small points of light. The phone's screen faces up at the roof; when it lights, its cool white glow falls on the roof lining and the inside of the windscreen, never into the lens.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a slightly chipped nail on one thumb.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.

AUDIO
Ambience: rain ticking on the car roof, a distant car passing on a wet road, the hush of a parked car.
Foley: two short vibration buzzes rattling on the dashboard plastic at 1 and 2 seconds, vibration only, no ringtone; the scrape of the case lifting off the plastic and a jacket-sleeve rustle at 4 seconds.
The incidental people do not speak. Any voices are distant and unintelligible, with no words that can be made out.
No dialogue. No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only at the head and the tail.

FINAL FRAME
The empty dark dashboard, rain on the windscreen, the wiper stopped part-way up the glass, camera holding.

Blue-grey early daylight through the car windows mixed with the warm amber of street lamps outside; the dashboard stays dark; his hands and the wheel are lit softly from the side window and fall off into shadow towards the gear lever; rain beads on the glass catch small points of light. Edit plan (what we do after hand-back)

Receipt grammar (every data moment): the exact crop of the real PNG on a navy #0B1628 card, 12 px radius; one thin orange #F7931E underline under the one figure that matters, with a soft tick; a slow 102% → 108% push-in over 3–4 s with a light grain match; the source line always on (Inter 500, #BDCBDC); a context strip where needed. No redraws, no count-ups, no up-arrows, no Google logos or colours on our graphics. Never "No.1", "#1", "first", "just hit", "now", "growth". Never the site's "No.1 Taxi Hire" headline.

Source line (all Search Console receipts): Google Search Console · goldenlinetaxiswarwick.co.uk · 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026 Context strip (positions): Average position over 3 months. Positions 1–10 are page one.

What this video is

  • Concept. After the last airport run, the owner sits down at his own kitchen table, pulls the laptop in and sees his three months of Google numbers for the first time. T1's real recorded voice talks him through it from the laptop speaker. One person on camera; his reactions are cut to the exact moments each number appears.
  • Hook. 16:9: the keys clatter on the table, he pulls the laptop in, and T1's voice comes out of the speaker: "Right, so this is your last three months on Google." 9:16 duet: the real totals tile (224 clicks · 15.9K times shown) is on screen in the top half by 0.8 s; his face leans in below.
  • Why this brand. Coventry Airport Taxis 247 has a clean, attributed Search Console screenshot with honest airport-search rows: one search averaging page one (7.0), one shown 607 times that is still at 22.0. That lets the film be candid about what's working and what's next.
  • What the edit reveals. For the first 26 s the data is seen only on his laptop (our real screenshots keyed into the green screen). At about 26 s (59% of the 44 s film) the first receipt goes full frame: coventry airport taxi · avg 7.0, page one on average. His own approved line follows. The close is honest: airport transfers coventry was shown 607 times but averages 22.0, "so that's the next one".
  • Framing. "First look at three months", never growth. There is no comparison period (gate G5).

  • Row 1's on-screen label reads "the most clicks of any search", not "top search": its average is 13.6 (page two), so "top" could read as a ranking claim.

Because his face is never seen there, the two colour temperatures meet across the back of his neck and shoulders, not on the face.

How to record a memo (send this to both of them):

  • One approved line per memo, three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take 5–8 s.
  • A quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom; not the kitchen, even though the film is set there). No TV, radio or music.
  • Phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way you'd say it on the phone to a customer, not read out.
  • Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

If the generated voice in A-02 or D-02 doesn't sound like him, it fails QC. We lay his real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

What this video is

  • Concept. At the end of a night shift the owner of Leam Taxis walks from his parked car to his front door, filming himself on his phone's front camera, and says the number in his own words: a hundred and fourteen calls off his Google listing, May to October. At his door he adds the best month: September, twenty-five. Then he turns the key.
  • Hook. Frame 1 is already his face mid-step, with two short buzzes from a phone in his pocket. The real 114 headline crop is on screen by 0.8 s with its source line, and a 0.6 s flash of his hand slamming the car door gives the first beat.
  • Why this brand. A running total is the one milestone this data proves without a comparison period: 114 calls made from the Business Profile, May–Oct 2026 (October part month), with September the best of the six months shown at 25 (read exactly from the tooltip). A taxi owner would say that number out loud. It also sets up V09's stitch ("…twenty-five").
  • What the edit reveals. The real headline crop lands first. The real chart then wipes on left to right above him as he walks (the real pixels revealed, never redrawn). On his word "twenty-five" we punch in on the real September tooltip with the caption September: 25 calls, the best of the six months shown. No growth claims, no "first", no "now".

Changes from the plan (one line each):

  • The pocket buzz moves from second 3 to second 0. The hook needs it on frame 1, and this keeps it out from under his line. It is two short message buzzes, not a ringing call, because a call he ignores breaks the "no call-ignoring" fix (§11).
  • Shooting order puts v03_B-01 first. It is hands only and tests the car and night street before his face is generated (master_plan §7: "QC the World Bible on the b-roll first").
  • Framing puts his face in the lower-middle of the frame, with the street filling the top 40%. That leaves room for the receipts in the upper band inside the safe zone, so the selfie line "top of the head nearly touching the top of the frame" is not used.
  • v03_S-02: §2.2 has no porch line, so the plan's "porch light is the key" is written as one new light line. It is pasted verbatim in S-02's still and video.
  • v03_S-02: his key is already in the lock in frame 1 (the plan has keys in his free hand). That keeps the last 2 s to one action: he turns it.
  • v03_B-01: the PHONE-REAR optics block says 1–2 m. Here it reads about 70 cm, because the shot is a close-up of the door.
  • The car is his own real car, so every prompt carries [CAR COLOUR] (see "Set once" below). The plan says "plain dark saloon"; his real car decides (character file).
  • The chart wipe uses the chart-only crop 15,265,910,210, because the headline is already on screen. The headline-plus-chart crop 15,165,910,310 becomes the end card (V09 reuses it for its end card).
  • Context strip added: Leam Taxis' Business Profile, confirmed by [Name], [date]. The screenshot shows no business name (§1.2 pattern, Gate G3).
  • Fallback IDs: v03_GL-01_9x16 comes from the character file. The no-face walk gets the new ID v03_P-01_9x16, because the plan names it but gives no ID.
  • v03_B-01 and v03_P-01 show no face, so their light line drops the World Bible's face and head-and-shoulders clauses, following the faceless v04_P-01 quality bar in master_plan §8.3.
  • Night prompts (B-01, S-01, S-02, P-01): PAL-EXT and the VEHICLE lock stay word for word, each followed by one night sentence (Tonight the low cloud is dark, faintly lit by the town. / Here it stands at the kerb under the street lamps, their reflections stretched across its wet panels.), the same way V05 handles its night yard, so the lamps stay the only light. GL-01 is daytime and needs neither.

DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. These are line shapes only. He rewrites them in his own words and records them, and only his approved words go into Seedance. Until then the prompts carry [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT] and [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT].

Questions to send him (he answers in one relaxed memo, MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_interview.m4a, 1–3 minutes):

  1. "Your Google listing shows a hundred and fourteen calls made from it, May to October. How would you say that to another driver?"
  2. "September was the busiest of those six months for calls: twenty-five. How would you put that?"

We transcribe his answers, pick one line for each shot, and he approves them in writing. Then he records each line as its own memo.

Shot Starts at (in the clip) Line shape (he rewrites) Length Memo file
v03_S-01_9x16 second 1 "A hundred and fourteen calls off our Google listing, May to October." 5–6 s, ends by second 7 MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line1.m4a (+ _outdoor)
v03_S-02_9x16 second 1 "September was the best of the lot. Twenty-five." Then a small laugh (not in the memo) about 4–5 s, ends by second 6 MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line2.m4a (+ _outdoor)

Rules for his lines:

  • The only numbers he may say are "a hundred and fourteen" (May to October) and "twenty-five" (September), said as words, exactly as the receipts show.
  • He may not say "first", "now", "just hit", "number one", "best month since May", "since May", "more", "up" or any other growth word. October is a part month, so it is never a drop.
  • "Calls", not "customers" or "people": the receipt counts calls made from the profile.
  • No review wording and no customer names. No "Hulk did this" or "the agency got us": no causal lines (G2, §1.5).
  • If he changes the wording, the numbers stay exactly as they are.

How to record a memo (send this to him):

  • Only after G3 clears.
  • One approved line per memo: three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes. Each take is 5–8 s at most.
  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen or the car). No TV, radio or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth (production_rules A.3), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way you'd tell a mate, not as if you're reading it out.
  • Then record both lines a second time outdoors, on your phone at arm's length while walking slowly on your street, and save them as MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v03_line1_outdoor.m4a and ..._line2_outdoor.m4a. These give us the real phone-microphone sound for the final track.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where: the clean indoor take is the @Audio 1 reference in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in his real voice (_outdoor first, or the indoor take with a light phone-mic EQ) wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, that is a QC fail (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

LIGHTING
Cold white LED street lamps mixed with one older amber lamp further down the street are the only light; wet pavement reflects both. Each lamp throws a pool of light on the pavement and house fronts that falls off into dark gaps between the lamps, and the warm lantern by the door is the brightest point as he nears it.

AUDIO
Ambience: a quiet terraced street at night in drizzle: rain on parked cars and hedges, a gutter dripping, a car hissing past on a wet road one street away.
Foley: footsteps on wet paving throughout, one splash through a puddle at 2 seconds; keys chinking in a pocket with each step; his footsteps changing from paving slabs to the front path at 6 seconds; his footsteps stopping on the doorstep at 7 seconds.
No dialogue and no voices.
Sound from the phone's microphone: footsteps, slight wind rumble outdoors, close handling noise.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
The plain front door, shut, under the lit wall lantern, drizzle in the warm light, the camera holding with a small sway.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted autumn colour as it really looks: wet slate greys, an overcast white sky, wet black tarmac, red-brick terraces and cream stucco, cold white LED and older amber street light; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. Tonight the low cloud is dark, faintly lit by the town.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. The door has no house number, no name plate and no lettering on the letterbox.
A plain [CAR COLOUR] saloon or people carrier with no livery, no door lettering, no roof sign text, no decals. The front and rear number plates are angled away from the camera, out of focus, or hidden behind a foreground object. It waits at a kerb, a driveway or a drop-off zone, never on a rank.
Nobody visible anywhere: no hands, no faces, no reflections of people, windows dark or curtained.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.
  • QC (pass/fail):
    • Walks like a person: a real step bob, a turn with inertia, a small sway at the end. No glide, no drone or gimbal float. Fail (gimbal-smooth) → the handheld line is in; remove "slowly" from the camera line. Then shorten to 8 s and change 7-10s: He stops on the doorstep; to 7-8s: He stops on the doorstep; (our P-01 cut then runs 0.0–8.0 s, with the receipts full frame from 8.0 s).
    • Street truth: no readable house number, sign or plate; no rank, roof sign or livery; the architecture matches his real street photos, not a film set. Fail (gibberish digits) → region edit, then blur. Fail (looks like a game level: every surface clean, even light) → add two dressing anchors (a recycling box, a bike chained to a railing) and heavier drizzle, then regenerate.
    • Nobody in it: no hands, no person in a window, no reflection in a car. Fail → keep the count line, then region edit.
    • Sound: footsteps in time with the bob, the change in footsteps onto the path, no voices, no music. Fail (music) → we mute it and rebuild the ambience.
    • Privacy: a neighbour could not recognise the house. Fail → use his photos for layout and materials only (see "Set once") and regenerate.

What this video is

  • Concept. Two plates filmed from exactly the same spot in a parked car, in exactly the same flat grey light. "May": the phone sits dark in its vent mount while the driver's fingers drum on the wheel. "August": the same frame, but the phone lights up twice and the hand lifts it out of the mount. The car never moves. Because the light, the rain and the framing are identical, the only difference the eye can find is activity.
  • Hook (0–2 s). Split screen, May beside August, with the hook card May: almost nothing. August: 32. on screen from the first frame (the plan's wording; see the proposed change under "Exact on-screen wording").
  • Why this brand. The Coventry Business Profile screenshot is the only real before-and-after inside one dated screenshot in the whole data set: almost nothing in May, the August marker sitting on the 32 gridline, 79 interactions in total. No archive or comparison export needed; we type only the printed 79 and the 32 gridline the August marker sits on.
  • What the edit reveals (14–22 s). The real Business Profile chart rises between the two plates and is revealed month by month, in step with the plates. The May and August markers are ringed. The card says honestly that these are interactions, not just calls, that the line peaked in August, then settled, and that October is a part month.

Deviations from the plan (one line each):

  • The phone sits in the centre vent at frame left, not "at frame right": from the passenger seat, only a centre-vent phone turned towards the driver keeps its screen edge-on to the lens (the same geometry as BR01_9x16).
  • The left hand drums in May and lifts the phone in August (the plan says the right hand drums): the left hand is the one next to the centre vent, so the action and the phone share one crop for the split screen.
  • The wiper rests along the base of the windscreen and returns there after its sweep, instead of "parked mid-glass": a single real wipe always parks at the bottom.
  • The wiper sweep now has a visible cause: the driver flicks the stalk once (physics: cause before effect).
  • A CAMERA block is added to the §8.3 worked prompt (it was folded into FORMAT MODE). The skeleton requires it.
  • L-CAR-DAY drops "on that cheek", because no face is in frame (as §8.3 already does). The phone's glow is a second sentence after the unchanged light line.
  • P-02's timeline gets a 2–3 s stage ("the light goes out") and a 7–8 s hold. The plan left 2–3 s and 7–8 s empty, and every range must be continuous.
  • In the 9:16 hook the split is top and bottom, not left and right: a left/right split of a vertical frame leaves two 540 px strips, too thin to hold the hand and the phone together. The 16:9 keeps left and right.
  • The 16:9 end beat uses v04_B-01_9x16 in the series' "phone clip beside receipts" layout. The plan has no 16:9 B-01, and no extra generation is needed.
  • When the owner's optional voice plays (22–25 s), the label switches to the §1.3 tier for a real voice over faceless footage: Dramatised visuals. Real voice, real data.
  • The 32 gridline label inside the real screenshot is underlined, so viewers can see where the hook's "32" comes from. Nothing is redrawn.
  • Memo distance is about 30 cm (production_rules A.3 and the character file), the same as every other file, not 20 cm.

Rules for his line: no numbers (the numbers are ours, on screen, with a source), no growth words ("kept climbing", "up", "doubled", "more and more"), no "No.1" or "first", no review wording, no "Ali". It must stay true after August, because the chart settles after August.

How to record the memo (send this to him):

  • One line per memo. Three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
  • A quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or a bedroom). No TV, radio, music or open window.
  • Phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, mono. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way you'd say it to a customer on the phone, not as if you were reading it.
  • Send it full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • File name: MEMO_CLIENT_COVENTRY_OWNER_v04_line1.m4a.

His face stays above the top edge of the frame and never enters it. The seatbelt is off and hangs slack; the jacket creases where the forearms rest, and the seat fabric dips under his weight.

0-1s: Ambience only. Both hands rest on the wheel; the phone is dark. End state: still.

Flat overcast daylight through the windscreen is the only key, soft and slightly cool; the side window camera-right adds a brighter edge; the cabin roof and footwell fall into soft shadow; the windscreen itself is slightly overexposed.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a plaster on one knuckle.

Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

Nobody speaks, inside or outside the car; no voices at all.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close cabin sound, faint road noise outside.
No dialogue. No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only at the head and the tail.

The driver's hands resting on the wheel, the phone dark in its mount, fresh drizzle beads on the cleared windscreen, camera static.

Centre: the lower half of the steering wheel with the driver's hands on the rim. Top third: the lower windscreen with drizzle, a faint band of condensation along its bottom edge and the wiper blades resting along its base; beyond it, soft and grey, the edge of the wet bonnet, a wet kerb with a puddle along the gutter, a concrete barrier and the rise of a ring-road slip road with a lamp post. Right edge: the door pillar and the driver's door window with rain beads. A parking ticket lies face-down and a little crooked on the dashboard by the windscreen.

The first visible frame already contains the driver's hands on the wheel and the dark phone in its mount; no empty establishing frame.

His face stays above the top edge of the frame and never enters it. The seatbelt is off and hangs slack; the jacket creases where the forearms rest, and the seat fabric dips under his weight.
The left hand rests on the rim at eight o'clock, within 30 centimetres of the phone, both left of centre; the right hand rests at four o'clock. The top edge of the frame runs across the middle of the windscreen and across the driver's chest. The phone is dark, its screen turned towards the driver.

0-1s: Ambience only. Both hands rest on the wheel; the phone is dark. End state: still.
1-4s: The fingers of the left hand drum slowly on the rim, index finger to little finger, stop for a beat, then drum again; the right hand stays still. End state: the left fingers resting on the rim.
4-5s: At second 4 the left hand slips behind the rim and flicks the wiper stalk down once; the wiper starts to lift off the base of the glass. End state: the wiper halfway up the windscreen, the fingers leaving the stalk.
5-6s: The wiper finishes its single sweep, drags the drizzle into a smeared arc and drops back to rest along the base of the windscreen; the left hand returns to the rim. End state: left hand back on the rim, the wiper at rest, the glass cleared.

The fingertips press slightly into the rim and lift off it with a small delay; the jacket sleeve shifts on the forearm as the hand moves; the wiper rubber drags water in a smeared arc and judders once at the top of its sweep; drizzle beads gather again on the cleared glass and run in short trickles; the water in the bottle stays level; the car does not move.

Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

Nobody speaks, inside or outside the car; no voices at all.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close cabin sound, faint road noise outside.
No dialogue. No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only at the head and the tail.

  • The car: any ordinary car, parked legally at a kerb (never on a taxi or station rank), engine off, on an overcast day. Drizzle helps. Tape over the badge on the steering wheel. Dashboard screen off. Park so no number plate is visible through the windscreen, or keep it soft and far away.
  • The camera phone: rear main camera at 1x, Portrait mode and filters off. Stand it upright (9:16) on a rolled-up jacket on the passenger seat at the driver's chest height, about 1 m from the wheel, angled across to the wheel. Tap and hold on the wheel to lock focus and exposure. Do not touch it between the May and August takes. For the 16:9 pair, lay it on its side on the jacket, raised on a book so the lens stays at the driver's chest height.
  • The prop phone: in a plain dark case, in a centre-vent mount, turned to face the driver. Set it to vibrate only, with notification previews off. Its screen must never face the camera.
  • The driver: a plain dark jacket with the cuffs pushed back, no rings or watch, a plaster on one knuckle; head always out of frame. They sign the short hands-only OK first (presenter-extras.md §2) and are never named or captioned.
  • Takes (10 s each, same spot): "May": hands on the wheel, the left hand drums, one flick of the wiper stalk, phone dark. "August": someone rings the prop phone, hangs up after one buzz, rings again; on the second buzz the left hand lifts the phone out of the mount and up out of frame. Nobody speaks. End beat: hold the camera phone at dashboard height about 40 cm from the prop phone lying face-down, ring it, the hand turns it face-up, screen edge-on to the lens.
  • Save as: grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4, grp_v04_P-02RF_t1_9x16.mp4, grp_v04_P-01RF_t1_16x9.mp4, grp_v04_P-02RF_t1_16x9.mp4, grp_v04_B-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4.

Add-on 4b · York Cars: old homepage → live homepage (real captures only, no generation)

Two conditions, both required:

  1. York Cars confirms in writing who rebuilt the site and in which month (our only date, about Nov–Dec 2025, is inferred from upload paths and unverified; the live footer says "Designed by Xoom Media"; Hulk's portfolio lists York Cars) and agrees we may show both versions. No confirmation, no 4b.
  2. Real "before" captures. Our sandbox could not reach the Internet Archive (research/wayback_before.md: every request was reset or rate-limited). The captures have to come from your own browser, or from York Cars' or Hulk's own project records. We never mock up an old site.

It is a separate short, not part of the Coventry film: two different businesses in one 25 s film would blur whose data is whose.

Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

  • Sound: Seedance's native rain, taps, wiper and buzzes are the soundtrack, crossfaded by 4 frames at every cut so the rain never jumps. Soft ticks on the underline and the two rings. No music by default. If you want a bed on the 9:16 only, one sparse licensed track at least 20 LU under the native sound, out by 22.0 and never under his line. No trending or copyrighted audio.
  • His voice (Version A): his real memo laid in as recorded, lightly cleaned, no pitch or timing changes. Never a voice he hasn't heard and approved.
  • Captions: only his line (Version A), word-timed, white with a soft shadow, Inter, two lines at most. 9:16: a band at 62–70% height. 16:9: bottom centre of the right two thirds.
  • Disclosure: the label sits lower-left and small throughout (9:16 at about 76–79% height; 16:9 with a 40 px margin). Set the platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
  • 9:16 safe zones: all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins. Footage may run into the margins; text never does.
  • Loudness: 9:16 at −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP. 16:9 web master at −16 LUFS (our default; tell us if your site player wants −14).
  • Finishing: one grain value matched to the phone's sensor noise, one sharpen value, and one identical light grade on all five clips (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange), so May and August stay identical. Upscale once with Higgsfield upscale_video (ugc preset) only if you had to generate at 720p.
  • End card colours: the case study uses GRP orange #F7931E / blue #3FA9F5 on #0B1628, Inter. If the 9:16 goes out as Hulk Marketing, the rings, underlines and lockup switch to Hulk lime #C6FA61 on #121C17.
  • Never on screen: "calls" as the measure (it is interactions); any month value other than 32 and the total 79; "No.1", "#1", "first", "now", "just hit", "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups; the Slough review widget or "4.9 / 202", "15,000+", "4.6", "100+ reviews"; the site's stock fleet or headset-operator images; "Qoute"/"Relaible" pages; any "Ali" review; clocks or time stamps; any "we built" line.

What this video is

  • Concept. On a wet Saturday night the York Cars manager walks us from the yard, through the office door, into the dispatch room, where York's night runs through one room. It is built only from York Cars' own photos of their yard and office. Without those photos there is no V05.
  • Hook. A car door thunks in the wet yard on frame 1. The manager is already striding away from it, glances back at the phone filming them, and starts talking at second 1.
  • Why this brand. York Cars is a 24/7 private-hire firm whose website is built for local search: a page for each of 15 suburbs and villages and 13 airports, and 2,695 Google reviews shown on the site. A night-shift tour shows the real business behind those pages.
  • What the edit reveals. At 20 s (67%) the real review count from their own site lands as a receipt over the dispatcher's hands. At 24 s, over real York night footage, a capture of the site's navigation shows the location and airport pages. Both carry the caption Context, not an agency result. This is context about the client. It is not a result we claim.

Changes from the plan (one line each):

  • Shooting order puts v05_B-01 first: it has no identity and tests whether the dispatch room reads as real before the manager is generated (master_plan §7).
  • v05_W-01: the manager has just parked and shuts the driver's door at second 0. The car points away from camera with its rear behind the camera, so neither plate can face the lens.
  • v05_W-01: the operator walks 1.5 m behind and 0.5 m to the manager's right, and the manager glances back over the right shoulder. This is the plan's "a step behind and to the side", fixed to one side.
  • v05_W-01, v05_B-02, v05_P-01: §2.2's L-STREET-NIGHT line is pasted verbatim (in P-01 without its face clause, see below), followed by one sentence placing the yard's real lamps. Set it from their night photos ("Set once" below).
  • v05_W-02, v05_B-01, v05_P-02: the plan's SCREEN-SOFT is replaced by "every monitor angled away". A phone's deep focus can't blur a monitor 4 m away, and dispatch screens show customer addresses.
  • v05_B-02: the plan's "three-quarter rear" view would show the rear plate. The camera now stands level with the rear bumper, looking forward along the car, so both plates stay out of frame.
  • v05_B-02 is made only if York Cars confirms it fits child seats. Otherwise the shot implies a service we haven't verified. The edit works without it.
  • Edit: W-01 runs 0–12 s and W-02 runs 12–20 s, so line 2 finishes before the first receipt at 20 s. The plan had W-02 at 14–20 s, which would have cut line 2 short.
  • Receipt R1 crops only the line "Based on 2,695 reviews", leaving out the stars, the Google logo and the reviewers' cards (no star average, no reviewer names, no Google marks).
  • Fallback IDs v05_P-01 and v05_P-02 are new. The plan names the POV walk-round but gives it no IDs.
  • Voice memos: the phone sits 30 cm from the mouth (production_rules A.3), not 20 cm.
  • v05_P-01: L-STREET-NIGHT's face clause is replaced (each lamp lights its own pool of wet tarmac and the yard falls dark between them.) because nobody is in frame.
  • Night film: PAL-EXT and PAL-INT stay word for word, each followed by one night sentence (Tonight the low cloud is dark, faintly lit by the town. / At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass.). The VEHICLE lock is followed by Here it stands on the yard's wet tarmac, the lamps' reflections stretched across its panels. The plan's lines carry day words (white sky, daylight at the window, kerb).
