Script and voice memos

DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. Questions only. We do not write the manager's sentences. They answer in their own words, we transcribe, they approve, and only then do the exact words go into Seedance. Until then the prompts carry [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] and [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT].

Step 1: the interview memo. Send them the two questions. They answer both in one relaxed memo, 1–3 minutes, as long as they like: MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_interview.m4a.

  1. "What does a Saturday night look like here?" → line 1
  2. "What do customers ask for most?" → line 2

Step 2: we pick one line per question (5–6 s spoken, never more than 6 s, so it ends by second 7 of its clip), and they approve both in writing.

Step 3: they record each approved line as its own memo.

Shot Line Starts at (in the clip) Must end by Memo file
v05_W-01 (both ratios) [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] second 1 second 7 MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line1.m4a
v05_W-02 (both ratios) [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT] second 1 second 7 MEMO_CLIENT_YORK_MANAGER_v05_line2.m4a
v05_P-01, v05_P-02 (fallback) The same two memos, laid in by us in the edit, unaltered edit 1.0 s and 13.0 s n/a the same files

Rules for their lines:

  • No numbers at all. The numbers (2,695 reviews, 15 suburb and village pages, 13 airport pages) are ours, on screen, with their source.
  • No "largest fleet", "number one", "best in York", "most trusted" or "Happy Users". No customer, driver or reviewer names, and no review quotes.
  • No line about the agency ("Hulk got us…"): G2 is unresolved, and the film is context, not an agency result.
  • If they mention a service (airport runs, students, the station), it must be one the site already lists.

How to record a memo (send this to them):

  • One approved line per memo: three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap. Each take 5–6 s.
  • Record in a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or bedroom). Not the dispatch room with the radios on, and not the yard.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side so the breath doesn't pop.
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting, or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, in mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. Re-record any take that distorts.
  • Say it the way you'd tell a new driver on their first night, not as if reading it out.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • Their accent is never described anywhere in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where: the best take is @Audio 1 in W-01 (line 1) and W-02 (line 2). In the edit we lay their real memo in as the final voice wherever sync allows, with a light phone-at-1.5-metres EQ and the yard or room ambience under it. If the generated voice doesn't sound like them, it fails QC (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice they haven't heard and approved.

Seedance 2.5 prompt · 6,784 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the hands, the radios, the keyboard and the desk layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any text.
@Image 2: geography and materials of the firm's own dispatch desk only (the radios in their chargers, the desk surface, where the monitors stand); do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, signs or printed text in it.

SCENE CONTEXT
Late on a wet Saturday night in the dispatch office of a small York private-hire firm, a dispatcher's hands type a short burst on the keyboard, then lift a two-way radio out of its charger, and the radio crackles.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone held by someone standing at the dispatcher's right shoulder, about 50 centimetres from the front edge of the desk, a little above desk height, angled steeply down across the desk. Foreground: the scuffed front edge of the grey laminate desk. Midground: the two hands; the worn dark keyboard at the lower right; a row of three handheld radios upright in their chargers at the left; a white tea-stained mug with a chipped rim between them; a biro at an angle. Along the top edge of frame, 70 centimetres away: the flat feet of two monitor stands, the screens above the top of the frame and never seen; a coiled charger cable trailing off the back of the desk; half a closed dark ring binder at the right edge of frame.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains both hands in position; no empty establishing frame. The right hand rests on the keyboard at the lower right of frame, fingers curled over the keys. The left hand lies flat on the desk at the lower left, about 5 centimetres from the nearest radio. Only one person's bare hands and forearms are in frame, close, entering from the bottom edge: the cuffs of plain dark everyday sleeves at the wrists, no logos or printed text, five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. The fingertips press and flatten slightly on whatever they touch, and the forearm takes its weight on the edge of the desk.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held about 50 centimetres from the hands, a little above desk height. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld and nearly still by a person standing at the desk: faint micro-shake from their breathing, small horizon tilts corrected by hand, no gimbal smoothness.
At second 3 the frame drifts a few centimetres to the left to follow the hand to the radio, then settles.
Autofocus hunts once, briefly, as the radio lifts towards the lens, then locks.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. Both hands still; the fingers of the right hand rest on the keys. End state: hands still, the radio in its charger.
1-3s: The right hand types a short burst of about eight keystrokes, pauses, presses one last key firmly with the middle finger and lifts a centimetre off the keyboard. End state: the right hand hovering over the keys.
3-5s: At second 3 the left hand closes around the nearest radio and lifts it straight up out of its charger; the charger contacts release with a small click; the weight of the radio dips the wrist and the hand steadies it; the thumb settles on the side button. At second 4 the radio gives a short burst of crackle with a distant voice too broken to make out any words. End state: the radio held upright about 10 centimetres above its charger, thumb on the side button.
5-6s: The right hand settles back onto the keyboard; the left hand holds the radio still; ambience only. End state: unchanged.

PHYSICS
The fingertips press and flatten on the keys and each key travels and clicks; the desk takes the weight of both forearms; the radio has real mass, so the wrist dips as it lifts and the fingers tighten to steady it; the tea in the mug shivers and its thin steam wavers when the last key is struck; the biro and the coiled cable stay where they are.

LIGHTING
Fluorescent ceiling tubes are the key, flat-ish but real with a slight green-cyan cast; the dark window adds nothing; darker corners at the back of the room; the monitors face away and give off almost no light. The tubes overhead lay a soft, slightly green sheen across the backs of the hands and the laminate, with a soft shadow under each finger, and the back of the desk falls darker.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small office at night: a fluorescent tube buzzing faintly, a radiator ticking, rain against a dark window, a kettle settling after it has boiled.
Foley: keyboard clatter from 1 to 3 seconds ending on one harder keystroke; the charger's small click as the radio lifts at 3 seconds; a short burst of radio crackle and hiss at 4 seconds with a distant voice too broken to make out any words.
The incidental people do not speak. Any voices are distant and unintelligible, with no words that can be made out.
Sound from the phone's microphone: room tone, the keyboard close, the radio slightly harsh and thin.
No dialogue. No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
The radio held upright just above its charger in the left hand, the right hand resting on the keyboard, the feet of the monitor stands along the top edge, the camera nearly still.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The monitor screens stay above the top of the frame and are never seen; they give off almost no light. The radios' displays stay dark and blank; the key legends are too small and soft to read.
Exactly one person, seen only as hands and forearms; the face never enters the frame. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

    • Hands: five fingers, real knuckle creases, the ink mark, fingertips that flatten on the keys. The radio has weight (the wrist dips). In the upper half of the frame, 4 metres away along the back wall, the dispatch desk: a row of handheld two-way radios standing upright in their chargers at each end of the desk, two monitors on stands turned to face the right-hand end of the desk so only their plastic backs and stands are seen, and right of centre, at the back of the room, one dispatcher sits at a desk with their back to the camera, small in frame and softly out of focus: plain dark everyday clothes, no logos or printed text, a radio headset over one ear, a lanyard turned round so only the plain back of the card shows. At the left edge of frame, a plain board of hooks with car keys hanging on plain fobs, and below it the corner of a counter with a kettle, a wisp of steam rising from its spout. In the middle of the frame, 2 metres from the camera, an empty swivel chair with a dark coat thrown over its back. The lower third of the frame shows a worn grey floor with a grey cable taped across it. Fluorescent ceiling tubes are the key, flat-ish but real with a slight green-cyan cast; the dark window adds nothing; darker corners at the back of the room; the monitors face away and give off almost no light. The tubes run across the middle of the ceiling, so the room is brightest in the middle and the floor, the corners and the space under the desk fall into soft shadow. Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger. Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen. Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Every monitor is angled away from the camera; only its plastic back and stand are visible, and it gives off almost no light. Exactly one person visible: the dispatcher, seen only from behind. Seedance 2.5 prompt · 7,877 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the dispatcher's position and the room layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any screen content or text.
@Image 2: geography and materials of the firm's own dispatch office only (walls, desk, fittings, window); do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, signs, papers or printed text in it.
@Image 3: the dispatch desk with its radios and chargers only; do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens or printed text in it.
@Image 4: the left hand of the person filming: hand shape, skin and proportions only; ignore its grey background and flat sheet light; it appears only on the desk from second 9.

SCENE CONTEXT
Late on a wet Saturday night, just in from the yard, the manager of a York private-hire firm walks into the small dispatch office filming the way ahead on the phone in their right hand, crosses to the desk where the radios charge and stops there while the dispatcher works at the back. It starts with the door closing behind the camera, crosses the room, and ends at the desk with a burst of radio crackle.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: the phone held upright in the right hand of the person who has just come in, at chest height, starting just inside the door at the left end of the front wall and facing into the room. The room is about 5 metres wide and 4 metres deep. Lower third of the frame: a worn grey floor with a grey cable taped across it. Middle: an empty swivel chair with a dark coat over its back, 2 metres in. Upper half, along the back wall 4 metres away: the dispatch desk with a row of handheld radios upright in their chargers at each end of the desk, two monitors on stands turned to face the right-hand end of the desk with only their backs seen, and the dispatcher right of centre with their back to the camera. Left edge of frame: a plain board of hooks with car keys on plain fobs and the corner of a counter with a kettle that has just boiled. A dark window with rain on the glass and a crooked blind is on the right wall, just out of frame.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already shows the room from just inside the door with the dispatcher in position; no empty or black opening frame. Nobody stands between the camera and the desk.
At the back of the room, one dispatcher sits at a desk with their back to the camera, small in frame and softly out of focus: plain dark everyday clothes, no logos or printed text, a radio headset over one ear, a lanyard turned round so only the plain back of the card shows. They lean a little towards a monitor that faces away; a radio handset stands on its charger within reach. Their face is never seen.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held at chest height, pointing ahead into the room. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld by a person walking slowly: gentle vertical bob with each step, small horizon tilts corrected by hand, no gimbal smoothness.
The phone stays at chest height in the walker's right hand and points where they are going, then tilts down a little at the desk.
In the first second the auto white balance shifts slightly from the yard's cooler light to the green tint of the tubes, then settles.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. Behind the camera the office door swings shut on its closer and its latch clicks. End state: the camera still, just inside the door, looking into the room.
1-7s: The walker crosses the room slowly towards the left end of the desk, passing the empty chair with the coat on the right; steam from the kettle drifts up at the left edge of frame. End state: about half a metre from the desk edge, the radios close at the lower left of frame.
7-12s: The camera stops at the desk and tilts down a little; at second 9 the left hand of the person filming enters from the lower left of frame and rests flat on the desk edge beside the radio chargers, fingers spread, taking a little weight; at second 10 the dispatcher shifts in the chair and it creaks. End state: the hand flat on the desk at the lower left, the radios beside it, the dispatcher at the back.
12-14s: At second 12 a short burst of radio crackle with no intelligible words comes from the desk; the dispatcher reaches for a handset on its charger. Ambience only. End state: unchanged, the dispatcher's hand on the handset.

PHYSICS
Each step lands with weight on the hard floor and the frame bobs with it; steam from the kettle drifts up and thins in the tube light; the radios in their chargers rattle very slightly when the desk is touched; the office chair rocks back a little under the dispatcher and settles; the coat on the empty chair hangs still.

LIGHTING
Fluorescent ceiling tubes are the key, flat-ish but real with a slight green-cyan cast; the dark window adds nothing; darker corners at the back of the room; the monitors face away and give off almost no light. The tubes run across the middle of the ceiling, so the room is brightest in the middle and the floor, the corners and the space under the desk fall into soft shadow.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched; hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small dispatch office at night: a fluorescent tube buzzing faintly, a radiator ticking, rain against the dark window, a kettle settling after it has boiled, a radio hissing low on the desk.
Foley: the door closer's hiss and the latch click at 0 seconds behind the camera; the walker's own footsteps on the hard floor, close, from 1 to 7 seconds; keys chinking in a pocket; a soft press on the laminate at 9 seconds; the office chair creak at 10 seconds; a short burst of radio crackle at 12 seconds with a distant voice too broken to make out any words.
No dialogue. The incidental people do not speak. Any voices are distant and unintelligible, with no words that can be made out.
Sound from the phone's microphone: room tone, close footsteps, a little reflection off the hard walls.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
The left end of the desk, with its radios, close at the lower left of the vertical frame, the dispatcher above and to the right reaching for a handset, the camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. At this hour the window is black, with the room's tubes reflected in the wet glass.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
Every monitor is angled away from the camera; only its plastic back and stand are visible, and it gives off almost no light. The key fobs, the radios and the walls are plain, with no tags, rota boards or names.
Exactly one person visible in front of the camera: the dispatcher, seen only from behind. No extra people.
The only part of the person filming that is ever seen is their left hand on the desk from second 9.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

What this video is

  • Concept. One plain question on screen, "What was it actually like working with Hulk?", answered by Organic Fostering's director or registered manager at the table in their own office at Beaumont House on Chester Road. A mug of tea they actually drink. A bus passes soft in the wet window behind them. Adults only.
  • Hook. A plain question card (never a fake comment bubble) over real footage of Chester Road in drizzle with a bus passing (RF06, never a tram).
  • Why this brand. It is the set's one regulated, non-taxi client, and the evidence is structural and true: a postcode check on the site and a library of plain-English guides. No performance data exists, so the film makes no traffic, ranking or enquiry claim and shows no allowance figure at all.
  • What the edit reveals. After the answer, real dated captures of the live site: the postcode check (/areas-we-cover) and the guides index (/blog), then the card 61 pages · 32 plain-English guides, sourced to the sitemap, with the context line Site structure, not traffic results. Then their last line, a half-smile and a sip of tea.

Deviations from the plan (one line each):

  • Lengths are 30 s (16:9) and 29.5 s (9:16), not 25 s: their last line plus an unhurried sip needs 8.5 s, and each receipt needs about 2 s to be readable. Still inside your 20–30 s format.
  • The first receipt lands at 15.5 s (52%), not 64%: it has to follow the answer, not cut into line 2.
  • The site inserts come from new dated captures of /areas-we-cover and /blog (taken 22 Oct 2026), not from the homepage captures: the homepage shows live allowance figures (£20,837.44, £400.72) and photos of children.

Script and voice memos

DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. We send one question, never a sentence:

"What was it actually like working with Hulk?"

Step 1: the interview memo. The director answers in their own words, as long as they like, in one file: MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_interview.m4a. We transcribe it and pick three lines. They approve all three in writing before recording them.

What they may mention: the plain-English guides, the postcode check, what the work was like day to day. What they must not say: any number, any allowance or income figure, "24/7", the Ofsted grade (unless the PDF has been checked), any traffic, ranking or enquiry result, any carer's or child's name or story, "No.1" or "first".

Step 2: record the approved lines, one file per line, three takes in each file with a 2-second gap.

Memo file Shot Starts at (in the clip) Longest it can be On screen (16:9 / 9:16) Line
MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line1.m4a v06_A-01 (both ratios) second 1 6 seconds 2.5–8.5 s / 2.0–8.0 s [APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]
MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line2.m4a v06_A-01 (both ratios) second 7 6 seconds 8.5–14.5 s / 8.0–14.0 s [APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]
MEMO_CLIENT_OF_DIRECTOR_v06_line3.m4a v06_A-02 (both ratios) second 1 5 seconds 22.5–27.5 s / 21.5–26.5 s [APPROVED LINE 3 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]

If a chosen line runs longer than its slot, we pick a shorter one from the transcript; we never speed it up.

Version B instead: they approve a two-sentence written statement (no recording needed). We show it as text: [APPROVED STATEMENT SENTENCE 1] / [APPROVED STATEMENT SENTENCE 2].

How to record a memo (send this to the director):

  • One approved line per file, three takes in the same file, 2 seconds of silence between takes.
  • A quiet room with soft furnishings, door shut, away from the main road (not the office by the window).
  • Phone about 30 cm from the mouth, slightly to one side so breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1/48 kHz recorder), mono, one voice, no TV, radio or music. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way you'd say it to someone thinking of fostering on the phone: calm, unhurried, not read out.
  • Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Never WhatsApp.
  • Their accent is never described anywhere in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

If the generated voice in A-01 or A-02 doesn't sound like them, it fails QC. We lay their real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice they haven't heard and approved.

@Image 1: identity of the director of a small fostering agency (face, hair, build, wardrobe: a soft grey knit cardigan over a plain top, as photographed; lanyard card turned to face the body; no logos, no printed text). 100% matches the reference.

SCENE CONTEXT
On an overcast, wet late-October morning, the director of a small fostering agency sits at the table in their own office on a main road in Manchester and answers an interviewer's question about working with their marketing agency. It starts with a mug of tea held in both hands, turns as they set the mug down between lines, and ends with them sitting back after a bus has passed soft in the window behind.

LOCATION MAP
Camera on a tripod at seated eye height, about 2.5 metres from the director across the table, facing them and the window wall behind them. Foreground: the near corner of the table, out of focus, at the bottom left of frame. Midground: the director seated just right of centre; on the table a plain closed notebook with a plain pen on it, and a small potted plant with a few browning leaves. Background: a large window filling the left half of the frame and reaching behind the director's right shoulder, rain beads on the glass, a wet main road outside, soft and grey; a roller blind pulled a third of the way down, hanging slightly crooked; a radiator with chipped paint under the window. At the right edge of frame, the back of an empty office chair with a navy coat over it, cut off by the frame edge. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the director in position; no empty establishing frame. They sit just right of centre, about 40 centimetres back from the table edge, upper body facing the camera and angled slightly towards camera-left, eyes resting just past the left edge of the lens towards the interviewer. Both hands hold a plain pale-grey mug of tea at chest height, elbows on the table edge, a thin curl of steam rising from it. Lips closed. The road outside is empty.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 2 to 3 metres from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, zero obvious distortion, natural face proportions, background readable but softly out of focus.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the eyes; one small natural focus correction when they lean forward to set the mug down.
The framing holds the director and the window together for the whole clip.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. They glance down at the mug, lift their eyes back to the interviewer and take a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak.
1-7s: At second 1, @Image 1 the director says, in natural British English, "[APPROVED LINE 1 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]", unhurried and warm, the mug held low at chest height, blinking naturally and glancing down once mid-sentence before looking back. On the last words they lean forward and set the mug down on the table by their right hand. End state: the mug on the table, right hand still loosely on its handle, eyes back on the interviewer.
7-13s: At second 7, @Image 1 the director says, in natural British English, "[APPROVED LINE 2 FROM THEIR TRANSCRIPT]", hands resting together on the table, one small open-palm gesture of the left hand on the key words, well below the chin. At second 9 a yellow city bus passes along the road outside, from the left edge of the window towards their right shoulder, a soft moving shape through the wet glass, gone by second 12. End state: the last word spoken, a small involuntary nod.
13-14s: They sit back a few centimetres in the chair and hold, breathing, eyes on the interviewer; ambience only.

PHYSICS
The mug has weight in their hands and pulls the wrists down slightly; when it touches the table the tea surface shivers and settles; the cardigan sleeves slide back a little on the forearms as they reach forward; the lanyard swings once and settles against the cardigan, the card still turned to the body; the chair takes their weight and creaks as they sit back; steam from the mug bends and thins in the window light; outside, the bus's tyres throw a faint spray off the wet road and rain beads on the glass stay put.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small office room tone, a radiator ticking, light rain on the window, occasional traffic on a wet main road muffled by the glass.
Foley: the mug set down on the table with a soft ceramic knock at 6 seconds; a bus engine and tyres hissing on the wet road outside from 9 to 12 seconds, muffled by the glass and kept low under the voice; a chair creak at 13 seconds.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the director at seconds 1 and 7, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices.
Clean close dialogue as if from a clip-on microphone, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The director sitting back a little, hands resting on the table, the mug by their right hand, eyes on the interviewer, the wet road empty again in the window behind; camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The bus is a soft shape behind the wet glass with no readable destination, number or lettering and no people visible through its windows.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people, nobody on the pavement outside, and no reflection of anyone in the window.

Midground: an open plain notebook in the middle of the frame, both pages blank; the hands on it, entering from the lower edge, the cuffs of a plain dark navy jumper at both wrists. Top of frame, softly out of focus: the far edge of the table, a few browning leaves of a small potted plant at the top right, the bright edge of a window with a radiator under it along the right edge near the top. Window light from camera-right.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains both hands in position; no empty establishing frame. The right hand holds a plain pen, nib resting near the margin of the right-hand page, between a third and three fifths of the way down the frame; the left hand lies flat on the left-hand page, holding it open. No face in frame.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto lens character, camera about 1.5 metres from the hands, the hands and the pen nib sharp, the mug in the foreground and the room behind softly out of focus, close framing through lens reach, not proximity.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the pen nib and the right hand.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The hands are still; the nib rests on the page. End state: nib touching the paper.
1-3s: The pen draws one small tick in the margin, lifts, then draws one short straight line beneath it. No letters, words or numbers are written. End state: a small tick and one short ink line on an otherwise blank page.
3-4s: The right hand lays the pen down across the open page and slides to rest at the notebook's edge. End state: pen lying on the page.
4-5s: The left hand leaves the page and curls around the mug's handle without lifting it; hold. End state: fingers on the mug handle, steam rising.

PHYSICS
The nib drags on the paper with slight friction and the page dimples under its pressure; the page corner lifts a few millimetres when the left hand leaves it, then settles; the pen rolls a few millimetres before it stops; the mug stays where it is when touched; steam bends and thins in the window light.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-right is the only key; the left side of the hands and the notebook fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger.
Plain dark everyday clothes; no logos, no printed text. Each incidental person is only partly in frame, seen from behind or from the chest down, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a small office room tone, a radiator ticking, light rain on the window, occasional traffic on a wet road muffled by the glass.
Foley: the nib scratching on paper at 1 and 2 seconds; the pen laid down on the page at 3 seconds; a light tap of fingers on the mug at 4 seconds.
No dialogue and no voices. No background music. No subtitles.
Sound as recorded on the camera's microphone: close small sounds of movement, natural room tone, no echo.

FINAL FRAME
The pen lying across the open notebook beside a small tick and one short line, the left hand on the mug's handle, steam rising; camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The notebook pages stay blank except for one small tick and one short line; no letters, words or numbers anywhere on the page.
Exactly one person, seen only as hands and jumper cuffs; no rings, no watch. No extra people.
Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.
  • QC (pass/fail): the four checks of v06_B-01C_16x9, plus vertical layout: hands and nib between 35% and 60% of the frame height. Fail → remake the still with the camera tilted further down.
  • Save as: grp_v06_B-01C_t1_9x16.mp4

V07 · Four Ways to Say Kenilworth Taxi

Category (your format) UGC 7: "What I learned from SEO" selfie, 20 s
Brand · website Hulk Marketing (team) · hulkmarketing.co.uk, using Golden Line Taxis, Warwick data · goldenlinetaxiswarwick.co.uk
Placement Hulk Marketing social: Reels, TikTok, Shorts
Final length 20 s
Aspect ratio 9:16 only
Capture mode PHONE-SELFIE (T1 films themselves). Fallback only: PHONE-REAR
Cast IDs T1_SEO (Mode B: face and voice, rain-jacket outfit) · fallback only: EXTRA_MODE_C (anonymous hands) under T1's real voice
Generations Version A: 2 (v07_A-01_9x16 12 s, v07_A-02_9x16 10 s) · Fallback: 1, made only if triggered (v07_P-01_9x16 8 s, hands typing on a green phone) · No AI version, ever

What this video is

  • Concept. T1, the agency's SEO specialist, walks out of their real workplace in drizzle and tells their phone the most useful thing they learned this month. On the same taxi site, over the same three months, four ways of typing "Kenilworth taxi" sat at four different average positions: 6.7, 16.4, 8.6 and 8.5. Tiny wording differences behave like separate searches, so you check every variant.
  • Hook. The real row 4 receipt (kenilworth taxis · 6.7) is on screen by 0.5 s, and row 13 (kenilworth taxi · 16.4) snaps in under it at 0.8 s. T1 is already mid-step on the front camera.
  • Why this brand. Golden Line is the client with a verified Hulk footer credit and an attributed Search Console screenshot. These four rows are real, sit in one export, and need no comparison period. The lesson is true without any growth claim.
  • What the edit reveals. As T1 says each number, we punch in on their face and the real Search Console row for that wording drops into the upper band. Four real receipts end up stacked, with the gap between 6.7 and 16.4 plain to see. A 1.4 s real Kenilworth clip (RF03) sits under "sixteen point four" and hides the join between the two takes.

Changes from the plan (one line each):

  • Re-grip moved from second 6 to second 11 in v07_A-01. Second 6 is where line 2 starts, and a camera jolt during speech causes mouth mush (production_rules D.7).
  • VEHICLE lock added to v07_A-02, where cars pass and stop in frame; §2.10 puts the lock in every prompt with a car exterior. v07_A-01 has no car in frame, so it has no lock (a parked car added a plate risk and nothing to the story).
  • Bus shelter: the plan's "unreadable advert" becomes a shelter seen from its back, its advert panel turned away so only its plain grey metal back shows. An advert face is the strongest text magnet on a street.
  • Crossing: a signal-controlled crossing, because zebra crossings don't beep. Its push-button box (it carries a "WAIT" panel) is turned away from the lens.
  • Framing: the head sits in the lower-middle of the frame so the four receipts fit the upper band inside the safe zone. The selfie line "top of the head nearly touching the top of the frame" is therefore not used.
  • Receipts: a full Search Console row (1318 × 49 px) is unreadable at phone width. Each receipt therefore shows the row's real query cell and real position cell side by side, with a visible gap: two exact crops of the same row, nothing re-typed. The full-width rows appear on the post's cover frame. We use the §1.2 orange underline, not the plan's "ring", so V07 matches the series.
  • Light: L-STREET is pasted verbatim, plus one sentence per shot naming which side of the face is brighter. A flat overcast line on its own invites the even, shadowless "render" look. In the hands-only fallback P-01, its "soft shadows under the eyes and chin" becomes "soft shadows under the hands and the phone", because no face is in frame (as V13's H-01 does).
  • No breath vapour. It is a daytime shot at around 10 °C. The atmosphere is drizzle instead.
  • Fallback: given the ID v07_P-01_9x16 (the plan names the shot but gives no ID). The thumb types over the lower third of the green screen, which relaxes SCREEN-GREEN's "one brief tap", because typing is the action. The four corner dots stay clear, and we key around the thumb.
  • Memo distance: about 30 cm, as in production_rules A.3 and T1's character file, so every memo in the set is recorded the same way.
  • A-02 ends on the turn, not the step off the kerb. The last second held the beep, a glance back, the laugh, a full turn and a step, which breaks one-change-per-stage and smears the face in the second the end card uses. It now holds the beep, the laugh and the start of the turn. The cut ends at 20.0 s (clip 9.0–9.9 s).

Set once, then keep in every V07 prompt

  • Glasses: if T1 always wears glasses, add , their own glasses before the semicolon in every wardrobe line (stills and Seedance). If not, never mention glasses.
  • Deep skin tone: if T1's skin is deep brown, add this sentence straight after the light line in every still and Seedance prompt: Exposed correctly for deep brown skin so the highlights show natural sheen and the shadow side keeps detail.
  • Shelter side: the prompts put the road on screen-left and the building fronts on screen-right. Rules for the lines:

  • The only numbers allowed are six point seven, sixteen point four, eight point six and eight point five, each with its own wording. They are average positions over 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026.

How to record a memo (send this to T1):

  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop (production_rules A.3).
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • One line per memo: three takes per line, each saved as its own file (MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>_t1.m4a, _t2, _t3). Each take must fit its slot: lines 1 and 2 under 5 s, lines 3 and 4 under 4 s; if one runs long, say it a little quicker. We keep the best one as MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>.m4a.
  • Say it the way you'd tell a colleague over a coffee, not as if reading.
  • Then record all four lines a second time outdoors on the V07 pavement, phone at arm's length, walking slowly for lines 1–2 and standing at the crossing for lines 3–4. Save them as MEMO_T1_SEO_v07_line<n>_outdoor.m4a. We use them where they line up with the lips, and under RF03.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • T1's accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

At second 6 a dark saloon slows and stops side-on in the far lane at the stop line at the left edge of frame, its nose dipping as it brakes and settling back on its suspension. End state: line finished, lips closed, a half-smile, the road behind them still.
9-10s: At second 9 the crossing starts to beep; they give a small breath of a laugh through the nose with lips closed and start to turn their head and shoulders towards the road; the phone tilts with their arm and the bright sky edges into the top of frame. End state: head turned towards the road, a half-smile, the frame tilting.

PHYSICS
They stand with their weight on one leg and shift it once onto the other; the open jacket fronts hang still, then swing a little as they start to turn at second 9; drizzle beads darken the jacket shoulders; the passing vehicles' tyres throw thin spray that falls back onto the road; puddles in the gutter ripple after each tyre.
The car has real weight: suspension settles after it stops, tyres flex on the kerb, road grime along the sills, rain beads on the bonnet, reflections of the grey sky distort across the panels.

LIGHTING
Flat overcast sky as a huge soft source from above; soft shadows under the eyes and chin; wet tarmac reflects the grey sky; no direct sun. In this shot the open sky over the road behind them, a little to camera-left, lights the camera-left side of the face a touch brighter, and the other side falls a little darker.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.

AUDIO
Ambience: a town-centre crossing at lunchtime in drizzle: tyres hissing on the wet road, drizzle ticking on metal, distant traffic, a door closing somewhere across the road.
Foley: the hatchback's tyre hiss fading out at second 1; the van's tyre hiss and engine passing at second 3; a soft brake squeak and an idling engine from second 6; the crossing's rapid electronic beeping from second 9; a jacket rustle at second 9.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the SEO specialist at seconds 1 and 5, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; a small breath of a laugh through the nose at second 9, no words; no other voices.
Sound recorded by the phone's built-in microphone at arm's length: close voice with a little reflection off the building fronts, faint handling noise when the grip shifts, a little wind rumble.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The SEO specialist's head turned towards the road, a half-smile, the bright sky edging into the top of frame, the stopped car at the left edge, the frame tilting with their arm.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted autumn colour as it really looks: wet slate greys, an overcast white sky, wet black tarmac, red-brick terraces and cream stucco, cold white LED and older amber street light; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
Every vehicle is plain, with no livery or lettering, and passes or stops side-on, its number plates never facing the camera; each driver is never more than a dark shape behind the wet glass. The push-button box stays turned away from camera.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone front camera at arm's length: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

Seedance 2.5 prompt · 6,381 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the hands, the phone, the green screen with its four corner dots and the bus shelter in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any text.
@Image 2: geography and materials of the real bus shelter only; do not copy its camera angle; ignore any adverts or printed text in it.

SCENE CONTEXT
Inside a bus shelter on a grey, drizzly late-October lunchtime, someone in a dark rain jacket types four short lines into a note on their phone, filmed over their right shoulder on a second phone. It starts with the thumb hovering, runs through four short bursts of typing, and ends with the thumb resting on the side of the phone.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a second smartphone held about 45 centimetres behind and above the typist's right shoulder, pointing down and forwards at the phone. Foreground: the soft, close edge of the dark rain-jacket shoulder in the lower-left corner of frame. Midground: two hands holding a plain dark phone upright at chest height, its screen flat green. Background, mostly in focus: the shelter's rain-streaked clear glass back panel; through it a wet pavement, the kerb, an empty wet road and grey building fronts across the road, too far to read, every sign angled away or out of frame; the shelter's plain grey metal upright at the right edge of frame; drops hanging from the roof edge at the top of frame. The open side of the shelter is on camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains both hands and the phone in position; no empty establishing frame. The left hand cradles the phone from behind, fingers on the back, the left thumb along the left edge beside the screen; the right thumb hovers 1 to 2 centimetres above the lower third of the green screen; the right fingers support the back of the phone. All four corners of the green and their dark dots are visible. No face is ever in frame.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held about 45 centimetres behind and above the phone being typed on. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld from just behind the typist's right shoulder, held almost still: faint micro-shake and one small drift, no gimbal smoothness.
Autofocus hunts once, briefly, as the thumb comes close to the screen at second 1, then locks.
The camera stays still while the screen is in frame.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The thumb hovers over the lower third of the screen. End state: thumb about to touch the screen.
1-3s: The right thumb taps quickly across the lower third of the green in one short burst, lifts, and taps a second short burst. End state: thumb lifted, hovering.
3-5s: A third short burst of taps; at second 4 the thumb pauses, taps once further to the right as if correcting a letter, and carries on. End state: thumb lifted.
5-7s: A fourth short burst of taps, then the thumb lifts away and comes to rest on the right side of the phone, off the screen. End state: the whole green screen clear of the thumb.
7-8s: Ambience only. The hands hold still; a drop falls from the shelter roof edge in the background. End state: hands still, thumb on the side of the phone.

PHYSICS
The phone has weight in the left hand: the wrist dips very slightly with each thumb press and recovers; the thumb pad flattens a little on each tap; the jacket cuff creases at the wrist as the thumb works; rain runs down the shelter glass in thin lines; drops swell at the roof edge and fall.

LIGHTING
Flat overcast sky as a huge soft source from above; soft shadows under the hands and the phone; wet tarmac reflects the grey sky; no direct sun. The shelter roof shades the hands from above, so the brighter light comes from the open side of the shelter on camera-left; the hands and the phone are a touch brighter on that side and fall a little darker on the right. The street beyond the glass is brighter than the inside of the shelter, so the glass shows the street through it, not reflections.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a slightly chipped nail on one thumb.
Dark rain-jacket cuffs over plain mid-blue overshirt cuffs; no logos, no printed text. The person is only partly in frame, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: drizzle drumming softly on the shelter's roof panels, tyres hissing past on the wet road out of frame to the right, distant traffic.
Foley: soft keyboard tap clicks from the phone in short bursts from seconds 1, 2, 3 and 5; a jacket cuff rustle at second 6; a single drip landing on the pavement at second 7.
No dialogue and no voices.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close shelter sound, the drumming roof, slight wind rumble, no voices.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
Both hands still, the phone upright at chest height, the thumb resting on its right side, the whole green screen and its four corner dots clear, rain running down the shelter glass beyond.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted autumn colour as it really looks: wet slate greys, an overcast white sky, wet black tarmac, red-brick terraces and cream stucco, cold white LED and older amber street light; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The phone screen shows a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill from edge to edge, evenly lit, with no interface, no text, no reflections and no glare; all four corners and the bezel stay visible, with one small dark dot in each corner of the green. The screen gives off almost no light. The thumb only ever covers the lower third of the screen; all four corner dots stay visible throughout.
Exactly one person, seen only as a shoulder edge and two hands; no face and no reflection of a face in the glass or the screen. No extra people.

Slot in the cut Line Matches on screen Memo file

Rules for the lines: impressions are always "times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched". Never say "number one", "first", "now", "up" or "growth", and never say "we built" or "our client". If T1 rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as written. Each line must fit in 5.5 seconds at a relaxed pace, which all five do.

Delivery: candid and unhurried, like showing a colleague something on your screen. The last line is plain and flat, not a punchline.

How to record each memo (send this to T1):

  • One line per memo. Three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between them.
  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings (a lounge or a bedroom, or a meeting room with the door shut). Not the kitchen, a stairwell or the open office. No TV, radio, music or open window.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (iPhone: Settings → Apps → Voice Memos → Audio Quality → Lossless), or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder, in mono. Speak at normal volume. If a take sounds distorted or clipped, record it again.
  • Read the numbers exactly as written ("seventy-six", not "seven-six").
  • Send the files full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • File names: MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line1.m4a to MEMO_T1_SEO_v08_line5.m4a. Tell us which take you prefer in each file.

Seedance 2.5 prompt · 7,726 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, desk layout, the laptop with its green screen and four corner dots, the mug and the hand's position in frame one; frame one matches this exactly; do not copy any text.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast morning someone at an ordinary office desk films their own open laptop on the phone in their left hand, while their right hand scrolls slowly on the trackpad. It starts with the hand resting, turns on two slow scrolls and one brief focus hunt, and ends with the hand settled on the palm rest.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone held in the person's left hand at their chest height, 55 centimetres from the laptop screen, from their own seat just above and behind the keyboard, angled slightly down at the screen. Foreground: at the lower-left frame edge, 25 centimetres from the lens and cut in half by the frame, an orange enamel mug with a small chip on the rim, a thin thread of steam rising from it; the near edge of the desk along the bottom of the frame. Midground: the open laptop in the middle of the frame, its screen a little above centre and filling about two thirds of the frame width; below it the keyboard deck and the trackpad; the right hand on the trackpad, entering from the bottom-right edge. Background: the pale grey wall behind the desk; at the upper-left, the edge of a large window with rain on the glass, a grey sky beyond and a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked across its top. A white charging cable runs from the laptop's left side across the desk and over its edge; a plain grey notebook lies face-down at the right edge, cut off by the frame. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the laptop with its green screen, all four corner dots visible, and the right hand on the trackpad; no empty establishing frame.
Only one person's bare hand is in frame, close, entering from the bottom-right edge, the forearm in a plain mid-blue overshirt sleeve with its cuff at the wrist, no logos or printed text, five fingers, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. The fingertips press and flatten slightly on whatever they touch, and the forearm takes its weight on the edge of the desk.
The index and middle fingers rest on the lower half of the trackpad; the thumb rests against the palm rest. The other hand is out of frame, holding the phone. The hand stays below the keyboard's top row and never touches or crosses the screen.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held at chest height 55 centimetres from the laptop screen. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep focus across the screen and keyboard, the mug nearest the lens slightly soft, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
The phone is held in the person's own left hand with the elbow resting on the desk; the frame is near-static, with slight handheld micro-shake and the small rise and fall of their breathing, never gimbal-smooth.
Autofocus hunts once, briefly, at second 5, then locks.
Exposure holds on the screen and the desk; the window at the upper-left stays slightly overexposed.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The hand rests on the trackpad; the screen is flat green and still. End state: still.
1-4s: The index and middle fingers slide slowly up the trackpad about 4 centimetres, lift, drop back to its lower half and slide up once more: one slow two-stroke scroll. The screen stays flat green. End state: the two fingers resting near the top of the trackpad.
4-7s: The fingers lift a few millimetres, hover, then settle again; the thumb shifts against the palm rest. At second 5 the autofocus hunts: the screen edges and the four corner dots soften for a moment, then snap back sharp. End state: sharp again, fingers resting.
7-10s: The two fingers slide down the trackpad once, a short, slow stroke of about 2 centimetres, and stop. End state: fingers resting at the middle of the trackpad.
10-13s: The hand lifts off the trackpad and settles flat on the palm rest to its right, the cuff dragging slightly on the metal. At second 11 the left hand re-grips the phone: the frame dips a few millimetres and recovers. End state: the hand resting on the palm rest, the frame steady.
13-14s: Hold; ambience only. End state: unchanged frame.

PHYSICS
The fingertips flatten slightly against the trackpad and the skin creases at the knuckles as the fingers curl; the cuff fabric folds and drags a moment behind the wrist; the laptop never moves and the lid holds its angle; the steam rises from the mug, breaks up and drifts slowly left towards the frame edge, never across the screen; rain beads on the window gather and run down in short jerks.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the hand and the keyboard fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The laptop screen gives off almost no light.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the back of the hand; a slightly chipped nail on one thumb.
The cuff of a plain mid-blue overshirt; no logos, no printed text. The person is only partly in frame, and their face is never seen.
The hand relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers.

AUDIO
Ambience: small office room tone, rain pattering on the window to the left, a radiator ticking, a kettle rumbling faintly in another room, distant traffic on a wet road.
Foley: the soft whisper of fingertips sliding on the trackpad from 1 to 4 seconds and from 7 to 8 seconds; the cuff brushing the palm rest at 10 seconds; the faint rub of the phone case against the fingers at 11 seconds.
No dialogue. No voices, near or distant.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close room tone, faint handling noise when the grip shifts, the rain on the window a little thin and distant.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only at the head and the tail.

FINAL FRAME
The laptop's flat green screen in the middle of the frame with all four corner dots sharp, the hand resting flat on the palm rest, the mug's chipped rim and a thread of steam at the lower-left, rain on the window at the upper-left, the frame steady.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.

The keyboard's key legends are worn and too small to read; the laptop has no logo and no stickers; the orange enamel mug is plain, with no print.
Exactly one person visible, seen only as one hand and forearm; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere. No extra people.

B2 · Real footage: film the three shots yourself (about 20 minutes)

A real hand on a real desk beats generated hands every time. The plan prefers this to generation.

  • Whose hand: T1's own, or a consenting colleague's after the short hands-only OK (presenter-extras.md §2). Wear a plain mid-blue overshirt. No watch with a logo, no rings. A real plaster or chipped nail is fine.
  • The desk: your real desk by a window, on a grey day. Use the orange enamel mug with hot tea, so it steams. Run the charging cable across the desk, and lay a notebook face-down. Turn every paper over, put tape over the laptop's logo and any stickers, and take nothing off the walls just for the shot (never dress the room up as a bigger office).
  • What's on the laptop screen. Pick one option:
    • Option 1 (recommended, simplest): a flat green full screen. Open a new browser tab, type data:text/html,<body style="margin:0;background:rgb(0,177,64)"> into the address bar, press Enter, then go full screen (F11 on Windows, Ctrl+Cmd+F on a Mac). Turn on Do Not Disturb first. In Chrome on a Mac, untick View → Always Show Toolbar in Full Screen. Set the screen brightness to about 40% so it doesn't light the hand green. We track the real corners of the bezel and key in the real screenshot, exactly as for the generated clips.
    • Option 2 (fully in-camera): open our receipt file coventryairporttaxis247_gsc_3m_full.png in the browser at 100% (we'll send it), go full screen, and scroll it for real. Start below the Search Console header, so your account picture never shows. Do not film the live Search Console: its numbers move day to day and must match gsc_data.json exactly.
  • The camera phone: rear main camera at 1×, held upright (9:16) in your left hand, elbow on the desk. Portrait mode, filters and the flash off; video at 1080p, 25 or 30 fps. Don't lock focus: one natural focus hunt is welcome.
  • The takes:
    • P-01_RF (14 s): from your seat, about 55 cm from the screen. Hand resting, two slow scrolls with a pause, then the hand settles on the palm rest.
    • P-02_RF (6 s): start on the laptop's lower-left corner, then swing slowly up and left to the rainy window and the mug, and hold.
    • P-03_RF (8 s): about 40 cm from the screen, angled down over the keyboard. One finger moves to the trackpad and taps once.
    • Nobody speaks. No music or radio in the room. Shoot three takes of each.
  • Save as: grp_v08_P-01RF_t1_9x16.mp4, grp_v08_P-02RF_t1_9x16.mp4, grp_v08_P-03RF_t1_9x16.mp4.

Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

  • Voice: T1's real memos, the chosen takes laid in as recorded. Light noise reduction and a gentle high-pass only: no pitch or timing changes, no AI voice repair. Never publish a voice T1 hasn't heard and approved.
  • Native sound: Seedance's room tone, rain, trackpad whispers, the click and the grip rubs stay. They sit about 15 dB under the voice, with 4-frame crossfades at every cut so the rain never jumps. Soft ticks on each underline move.
  • Music: none by default. It's a candid talk-over-a-laptop clip, and music makes it read like an ad. If you want a bed, use one sparse licensed track at least 20 LU under the voice, out by 28.0. No trending or copyrighted audio.
  • Captions: word-timed, white with a soft shadow, Inter, two lines at most, in the 62–70% band. Numbers appear as figures (6, 1 in 10, 76, 8, 7), with "just hit" in quotes.
  • Disclosure: the label sits lower-left and small throughout. Set the platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
  • 9:16 safe zones: all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins. Footage may run into the margins; text never does.
  • Loudness: −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP.
  • Screen key (master_plan §9):
    • Tracking: corner-pin on the four dots (in P-02 and P-03, a planar track on the visible dots plus the bezel edges).
    • Insert brightness: set it to about 85% white with a slight cool cast, so it sits in a daylit room rather than glowing.
    • Surface: a soft glare pass from the window side (left), a 1–2 px chromatic edge, faint moiré and a grain match.
    • Spill: a faint cool-white spill from the page onto the keyboard deck, the trackpad and the top of the hand (P-01, P-03), so the bright page reads as lighting the desk.
    • Match the camera: copy P-01's focus hunt at src 5–6 s (the insert softens with it) and every punch-in, and match the motion blur on P-02's swing.
  • Finishing:
    • One grain value matched to the phone's sensor noise, one sharpen value, and one light grade across all three clips (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange).
    • Upscale once with Higgsfield upscale_video (ugc preset), only if you had to generate at 720p.
  • Optional 16:9 reuse (Coventry case-study page, "phone clip beside receipts"):
    • Layout: the 9:16 master in a rounded phone frame on the left third of a 1920 × 1080 navy card. R6 (the full row 4) builds on the right two thirds at 0.9×, then R4/R5, with the source line and context strip under them.
    • Mix the web master at −16 LUFS.
    • It only goes live once G11's Coventry site fixes are done, if the page also shows the live site.
  • Never on screen: "No.1", "#1", "first", "now" as a claim, "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups; "people saw" or "people searched"; "last quarter"; "15,900" (it's 15.9K, and not used here anyway); the Coventry site's Slough review widget, "15,000+" or "4.6"; any "Ali" review; clock or time stamps; any credit line before G2.

What this video is

  • Concept. On a wet afternoon between jobs, the owner of Leam Taxis is parked on a Leamington terraced street (at a kerb, never on a rank), engine off, reading the monthly report on his phone. A second phone propped in his dash mount films him. The reaction is small: he reads, scrolls back to check, breathes out a short laugh, maybe says one word to himself, rubs the back of his neck and looks out at the rain. It is labelled as a re-creation.
  • Hook. A 1.5 s stitch of V03 (his "…twenty-five"), with the real September tooltip on screen by 0.8 s, then a hard cut into his car.
  • Why this brand. Leam Taxis' Business Profile shows 25 calls in September 2026, read exactly from the tooltip, the best of the six months shown. A September report is the one moment where that number lands, and V12 (T2 sending the report) and V03 (the owner's milestone) both lead into it.
  • What the edit reveals. The real tooltip is keyed into the green screen of his phone, then pushed to full frame with its source line. The end card is the real headline-and-chart crop with its own range, May–Oct 2026 (October part month). Never "best month since May", and never "114 calls since May" after a September report.
  • Best of all (plan): he films the real moment himself next month, and we use that instead (Version B1 below).

Changes from the plan (one line each):

  • The plan's table points to "worked prompt §9.2". The worked prompt is master_plan §8.2, which this file builds on.

Their words, their voice. Real data. It is true even if he stays silent in R-01, because the V03 stitch carries his own approved words and voice. With no V03 stitch and no word, it becomes AI re-creation made with [Name]'s permission. Real data.
  • R-01 framing: §8.2 says both "head and shoulders in the lower two thirds" and "the top of the head close to the top edge". These conflict, and the phone held low has to stay in frame. So his head sits in the upper part of the frame, near the top edge, with his hands and phone along the bottom.
  • R-01 final frame: §8.2 ends with "the phone lowered to his lap", but its timeline never lowers it. Lowering it as well as the neck rub and the turn would crowd one 3 s stage, so the phone stays low in his right hand at the bottom edge of frame to the end.

Script and voice memos

DRAFT FOR CLIENT APPROVAL. The reaction word is optional. If he'd rather not speak, R-01 is made silent (the no-word swap below), and the V03 stitch still carries his own voice. Until he approves a word, the prompts carry [HIS APPROVED WORD, e.g. Twenty-five.].

The question to send him (he answers in a short memo, MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_interview.m4a):

  1. "When you saw September's calls in your report, what did you say, if anything? One or two words, the way you'd say it to yourself in the car."

We transcribe it and suggest one word or a very short phrase. He approves it in writing, then records it as its own memo.

Shot Starts at (in the clip) Line shape (he decides) Length Memo file
v09_R-01_9x16 second 5 e.g. "Twenty-five." Said quietly, to himself, not to the camera about 1 s, ends by second 6 MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_line1.m4a (+ _car)

Rules for his word:

  • The only number he may say is "twenty-five" (September), said as a word, exactly as the receipt shows.
  • Never "best month since May", "since May", "first", "now", "just hit", "number one", "more", "up" or any growth word.
  • No "Hulk did this" or "the agency got us": no causal line (G2, §1.5).
  • A word that isn't a number ("Lovely.", "Look at that.") is fine too. The numbers stay on screen, from the receipt.

How to record the memo (send this to him):

  • Only after G3 clears.
  • One word or phrase per memo: three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen). No TV, radio or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth (production_rules A.3, as in V03), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Say it the way you'd say it to yourself, quietly, not as if you're reading it out.
  • Then record it once more sitting in your parked car, engine off, windows shut, phone in your dash mount about 55 cm away, and save it as MEMO_CLIENT_LEAM_OWNER_v09_line1_car.m4a. This gives us the real phone-in-a-car sound for the final track.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where: the clean indoor take is @Audio 1 in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in his real voice wherever sync allows (the _car take first). If the generated voice doesn't sound like him, that is a QC fail (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice he hasn't heard and approved.

SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held about 50 centimetres from the phone on the wheel. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

No dialogue and no voices.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close cabin sound, faint road noise outside.
No background music. No subtitles.

The phone upright on the top of the wheel in his right hand, the green screen clear with all four corners and dots visible, rain on the windscreen beyond, the camera almost still.

Send him this:

  • When: the next time his monthly report arrives. Only when you are parked at a kerb or on your drive with the engine off. Never on a rank, and never while driving.
  • Set-up: put your phone in your dash mount at chest height, front camera facing you. Use normal Video mode at 1080p, 30 fps. Portrait, Cinematic and beauty modes off. Seatbelt off. Wipe the lens.
  • Record: start recording before you open the report. Then open it and read it as you normally would. Read it on a second phone or tablet; the recording phone stays in the mount the whole time. Keep the screen pointed at you, not at the camera. Let it run for 10 seconds after you've finished reading. 30–90 seconds is plenty.
  • Say whatever you'd naturally say, or nothing. We only use the words you approve afterwards. If you read out a number, it must be from that report.

No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. The instrument panel is dark, with no lit dials, warning lights or numbers.
The phone's screen is never visible face-on. The engine is off and the car is parked at the kerb. Exactly one person, seen only from the chest down; his face never enters the frame, and there is no reflection of a face in the door glass. No other people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

    • Real weight: the silent laugh moves his chest and the phone dips; the phone lands flat with a dent in the fabric; the hand returns with weight. No floating hand, no sliding phone. Fail (floaty) → D.7: one action per stage. What this video is

  • Concept. Three short portraits from one wet October morning in the agency's real room. Each opens on the person's hands doing their real job (typing, sketching a report, making the tea), then a medium shot at their own desk where they say their name, their role and one true thing they do for a named client, then a small human tail (a laugh, a sip, back to work). It ends on one real number from a client they really worked on, shown as a receipt.
  • Hook. Hands mid-task, with that person's receipt number on screen by 0.8 s in the 9:16 cut.
  • Why this brand. It is the agency itself, on its own service pages. It shows real people doing real work, which the 30 sample portraits on googlerankerpro.com can't do. Hassan comes last and is just another person at a desk: his hands-first shot is him making the tea.
  • What the edit reveals. T1: 744 different searches Golden Line Taxis was shown for. T2: 25 calls from Google in September for Leam Taxis. Hassan: 312 clicks for Golden Line Taxis in three months (your pick; see the edit plan). Each is an exact crop of the real screenshot, with its source and dates.

Rules for the lines

  • T1's task must come straight from the Golden Line work log, in about eight words, so the whole of line 2 takes 5 s or less. No causal verbs ("made", "drove", "got them to"), no rankings, no numbers.
  • T1's name: say it in the form agreed in writing. If T1 is Muhammad Ali, agree a form that can't be confused with the "Ali" in Golden Line's duplicated reviews (G10), for example the full name.
  • No "No.1", "first", "now", "last quarter" or growth words in any line.
  • "I make the tea" stays only if it is true.
  • Each memo is one line. Lines must be said in 5–6 s at a natural pace. If a line runs longer, shorten the wording, not the pace.

How to record a memo (send this to each person)

  • Use a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not the kitchen or a stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music. In Pakistan, turn the ceiling fan off.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side, so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Use Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • One line per memo. Record three takes of the line, each as its own file: MEMO_<CASTID>_v10_line<n>_t1.m4a, _t2, _t3. We keep the best as MEMO_<CASTID>_v10_line<n>.m4a, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s.
  • Say it the way you'd say it to a colleague who asked, not as if reading.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • Nobody's accent is ever described in a prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where. The memo is the @Audio reference in Seedance (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like the person, it fails QC (production_rules G.1). Never publish a voice the person hasn't heard and approved.

QC each clip at full resolution with sound before you start the next. All three people share one room (L1), one light line, one palette and one texture line, so the set reads as one shoot.
