Seedance 2.5 prompt · 6,075 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: the SEO specialist's hands (skin, hand shape, nails, wrists, and the cuffs of a mid-blue overshirt over a plain white T-shirt; no logos, no printed text). Identity of the hands only; 100% matches the reference.
@Image 2: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the laptop, the mug, the sticky note and the desk layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any screen content or text.
@Image 3: geography and materials of their own desk and the window beside it only; do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, labels or printed text in it.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast late-October morning, an SEO specialist's hands type a short post on a laptop at their own desk by a rainy window. Only the hands are ever seen.

LOCATION MAP
Camera on a tripod at seated chest height, about 1.3 metres away at the front-left corner of the desk, angled across the keyboard towards the right. Foreground: at the left edge of frame, soft and close to the lens, an orange enamel mug with a chipped rim, a thin thread of steam rising and breaking up. Midground: a plain dark grey laptop on a worn wood-effect desk, its keyboard filling the middle of the frame at an angle, both hands on the keys. Top edge: the lower part of the laptop screen, out of focus, with a blank pale-yellow sticky note on the lower-left corner of the bezel. Background, compressed and soft: the pale grey wall; the corner of a plain grey notebook lying face-down at the right edge. A white charging cable runs from the laptop's left side across the desk and over its front edge. The window is just out of frame on camera-left, and its light falls across the desk from the left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains both hands on the keyboard; no empty establishing frame. The left hand rests on the left half of the keys; the right hand rests on the right half, thumb over the space bar. The wrists sit just above the palm rest, the overshirt cuffs at the lower edge of frame. The shoulders and face are above the top of frame and never enter it.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE. Camera static.

OPTICS
29° diagonal field of view, short telephoto lens character, camera about 1.3 metres from the hands, hands and keys sharp, background compressed and softly out of focus, close framing through lens reach, not proximity.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the fingers on the keys; one small natural focus correction when the right hand moves to the trackpad.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. Both hands rest still on the keys, as if the person is reading back what they wrote. End state: fingertips resting on the keys.
1-3s: Both hands type a quick burst: fingertips press and release the keys with short travel, the right thumb taps the space bar twice, the left little finger holds down a key for a capital letter. End state: hands paused mid-sentence, fingers hovering just above the keys.
3-4s: The right hand slides down to the trackpad, two fingers move a short way and click once, and the hand returns to the keys. End state: both hands back on the keys.
4-5s: The right hand types four more keys, then both hands go still. End state: hands resting on the keys, steam still rising from the mug.

PHYSICS
Each key dips under the fingertip and springs back; the wrists lift and settle slightly with each burst; the overshirt cuffs shift on the wrists as the right hand moves to the trackpad and back; the laptop stays put on the desk; the steam leans and breaks up in the faint draught from the window; the sticky note's curled corner trembles once when the right hand lands back on the keys.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the hands and the keyboard fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The laptop screen gives off almost no light.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: small office room tone, rain pattering on the window to the left, a radiator ticking, a kettle rumbling faintly in another room, distant traffic on a wet road.
Foley: soft plastic key clicks from 1 to 3 seconds; the duller thud of the space bar twice; one trackpad click at 3 seconds; four key clicks at 4 seconds.
No dialogue. No voices, near or distant.
Sound as recorded by the camera's own microphone close to the desk: the keys close and dry, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
Both hands resting on the keys, the orange mug steaming soft at the left edge, the blank sticky note soft at the top edge, camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The key legends are worn and too small and soft to read; the laptop has no logo and no stickers; the sticky note is blank; the orange enamel mug is plain, with no print.
The laptop screen sits out of focus at the top edge of frame, its picture a dim, soft blur with no readable detail.
Exactly one person, seen only as hands and wrists; no face and no reflection of a face in the screen, the mug or the window. No extra people.
Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast late-October morning, the agency's founder sets his mug of tea down at his own desk in a small office and tells an interviewer, drily, who he is and what every client gets. It starts with the mug landing, turns to the interviewer for two short lines, and ends with a small laugh, a sip, eyes back on the laptop.

LOCATION MAP
Camera on a tripod at seated eye height, 2 metres in front of the desk and slightly to the window side, facing the founder and the wall behind him. The interviewer stands just past camera-left, out of frame. Middle of the vertical frame: the founder seated a little right of centre behind a worn wood-effect desk; a plain dark grey laptop open at the right edge of frame, turned towards him so only the back of its lid faces the camera. Lower third: the desk top; a plain notebook lying closed by the laptop; a white charging cable looping over the front edge of the desk at the bottom of frame. Upper third, soft and open: the pale grey wall and, at the upper-left, the edge of a large window with rain on the glass and the lower edge of a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked; a radiator with chipped white paint under the window at the left edge, the shoulder of a navy wool overcoat hanging over a chair back beside it. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the founder in position; no empty establishing frame. He sits a little right of centre, the top of the head at about 38 percent of the frame height, the face in the middle of the frame, forearms and desk top in the lower third. Torso angled towards the laptop at the right edge of frame; eyes down on the orange enamel mug in his right hand, held 3 centimetres above the desk in the lower-left of frame, steaming; his left hand rests on the desk by the laptop; lips closed.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 2 to 3 metres from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, zero obvious distortion, natural face proportions, background readable but softly out of focus.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the eyes; one small natural focus correction as the mug comes up.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. He sets the mug down on the desk; it lands with a small knock and the tea ripples; he lets go and turns head and shoulders towards the interviewer just past camera-left, taking a small breath. End state: facing the interviewer, right hand resting beside the mug, lips parted, about to speak.
1-6s: At second 1, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "I'm Hassan. I co-founded Hulk Marketing, and I make the tea.", dry and matter-of-fact, eyebrows lifting slightly on "and I make the tea" as his eyes flick down to the mug and back. End state: line finished, lips closed, a small half-smile.
6-12s: At second 6, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "Every client gets their real numbers, with the context next to them.", steadier, his right hand opening a little above the desk on "context" and settling back, well away from the mouth. End state: line finished, lips closed, one small nod.
12-15s: At second 12 he gives a small breath of a laugh through the nose, no words, and his right hand lifts the orange mug. At second 13 he takes one slow sip, eyes going back to the laptop screen over the rim. End state: the mug held just below his chin, eyes on the laptop screen.

PHYSICS
The chair takes his weight and creaks softly as he turns; the jumper sleeve drags across the desk edge; the mug has real weight: it lands with a knock that ripples the tea, his wrist tilts as he lifts it, the steam bends as it moves; his watch slides a little on his wrist as the hand turns; the laptop stays where it is.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The laptop screen gives off almost no light.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched; a stray thread at one jumper cuff.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each, fingers not touching the face during speech.

Clean close dialogue as if from a clip-on microphone, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

The founder holding the orange mug just below his chin, eyes back on the laptop at the right edge of frame, the wall and rainy window soft in the upper third, camera holding.

What this video is

  • Concept. An honest look behind the scenes. Every case study starts with no numbers, just a site map. The hands lead: a marker squeaks out an empty box and an arrow, blank Post-its go onto a monitor, and blank index cards are laid out like a family tree beside a green laptop. Then one medium-wide two-shot of T1 and T2 at the whiteboard: T2 draws, T1 points at a gap, a low wordless murmur, one laugh, and the kettle clicks off next door.
  • Hook (0–0.8 s). The text card Day one. No numbers yet. is on screen from frame 1, over the first marker squeak.
  • Why this brand. Zentro is not a taxi firm, so it widens the agency's story. It also has no performance data on file at all: no Search Console, no Business Profile, no rankings. That is exactly what "day one" looks like. The only real thing we can show is the structure of the site, and that structure is real: 10 laptop brands and 3 phone brands, each with its own repair page.
  • What the edit reveals. The green laptop gets Zentro's real brand-repair page, keyed in from today's capture. We push into the screen, and the real brand grids fill the frame. Each brand tile is outlined one by one, then the card reads 10 laptop brands · 3 phone brands · a page each, with the source line and the context No performance data yet. The film ends on Ask us again in three months.

Deviations from the plan (one line each):

  • Shooting order is O-02 → O-03 → O-01 → O-04 (the shot needing no consent goes first, then the work is batched by set-up: desk, then whiteboard). The gen IDs don't change.
  • Hands-only twins O-01C and O-03C are added (Version B), because the plan gives O-01 to T2's hand and O-03 to T1's hands. The twins are anonymous Mode C hands, so the hands-only cut can be made today with no consent.
  • O-02's monitor is switched off (a dark matte screen with no picture) instead of SCREEN-SOFT. A phone 35 cm from a bezel keeps the screen in sharp focus, so a "soft" screen would be physically wrong. A switched-off matte screen gives the same result: no readable detail.
  • TEXT-LOCK is added to O-03 (production_rules §F asks for it in every prompt with a place). O-02 keeps the plan's PAL-INT without the AGENCY ADD-ON, because its orange Post-its already carry the orange.
  • L-OFFICE is adapted in the three hands shots ("the right side of the hand and the board fall a stop darker"), because there is no face in frame. It is verbatim in O-04.
  • The laptop insert is the real brand grid, static, not a scroll of now_desktop_full.png. That homepage shows the banned Zentro self-claims (5,000+ customers, 4.8/5, 2,560+ reviews) and the unsourced testimonials. Also, no hand touches the laptop in O-03, so a scroll would look like it moved on its own.
  • The receipts come from the brand grids on zentro.co.uk/laptop-repair and /mobile-repair. We captured them today, 22 Oct 2026. They print each brand's name and the site's own counts, "10 brands available" and "3 brands available". The open navigation-menu captures are kept as alternates. The source line now names those pages.
  • The Google "G" logo in Zentro's mobile grid: two options, your choice. (a) Leave the tile untouched: it is the site's own mark, kept as evidence (§1.2). (b) Desaturate the logo area to grey, so no Google colours show (§9 "no Google marks"). Either way the word "Google" stays. We default to (b) unless you tell us otherwise.
  • Hands-only stills use Nano Banana Pro, not Soul (team.md §5 gives Soul to solo anchor stills): there is no face to lock, and Nano Banana Pro follows the hand, desk and screen detail more closely.
  • The O-04 label drops "Their words, their voice." Nobody says any words in V11, so that part of the §1.3 label wouldn't be true.
  • The anonymous version says "a UK repair business", not "a Manchester repair business". Zentro publishes no address; Manchester is only inferred from its 0161 number.
  • The Golden Line fallback counts come from today's captures: 17 location pages and 8 airport pages. The live menu lists "Hampton Airport Taxi" twice (Hampton Lucy and Hampton Magna), so Golden Line fixes that label before we use the capture (G11).

The set (the same in every shot)

  • The room: an ordinary small office with pale grey walls and a large window on the left wall: rain on the glass, a grey sky, and a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked. A radiator, and a kettle within earshot.
  • The desk: a worn wood-effect top with a dark keyboard and a monitor on a plain grey stand. A plain dark grey 14-inch laptop with no stickers (the same laptop as V08), and a white charging cable over the desk edge.
  • The orange enamel mug with the small chipped rim: the agency's one brand-orange object, plain, hot tea, steaming. It sits at a frame edge in O-01, O-03 and O-04.
  • The whiteboard: plain white, slightly worn, with faint shapeless smudges of old marker. It has an aluminium frame and pen tray, a grey felt eraser, and plain dark markers with nothing printed on the barrel (peel or tape over the label if you're shooting real reference photos). Only empty boxes and arrows ever go on it: no words, no letters, no numbers, no client names.
  • Sticky notes: blank, square, pale yellow and orange. Index cards: plain white, unruled, blank.

Image prompt · 3,545 characters
A single vertical frame of smartphone video, recorded on a wet, overcast late-October morning at an ordinary desk by a window in a small office room. The filming phone is held by someone crouching just left of the desk, level with the bezel, about 35 centimetres from the lower-left corner of a computer monitor and angled slightly up at it. The monitor stands on a plain grey stand on a worn wood-effect desk and is switched off: its screen is a dark, matte charcoal surface with only a dull, shapeless sheen of grey window light on it, no picture, and no reflection of any person, phone or object. Its lower bezel runs across the middle of the frame from the left edge, slightly tilted, with a faint film of dust and a pale strip of old sticky residue where notes have been stuck before. Two blank square sticky notes are already stuck along the lower bezel side by side, a pale yellow one on the left and an orange one beside it, their sticky strips on the bezel and their lower halves hanging slightly away from it, the yellow one's lower corner starting to curl. Two bare hands enter from the bottom edge of the frame: the right hand's index and middle fingers press a third blank orange note onto the bezel 3 centimetres right of the other two; the left hand, lower and closer to the lens, holds a small square pad of blank yellow and orange notes. The cuffs of plain dark everyday sleeves at the wrists, no logos or printed text; five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. Below the bezel, the top edge of a dark keyboard whose worn key legends are too small to read, and a white cable running off the right edge of the frame. Above and behind the monitor at the upper-left, a pale grey wall and the edge of a large window with rain beads on the glass, slightly overexposed; fine dust drifts in the window light between the lens and the monitor. If a desk or monitor photo is attached, take only the desk, monitor shape, wall, window and materials from it and ignore any text, labels, logos or screen content in it; if a hands photo is attached, take only hand shape, skin texture and proportions from it, not an identity. Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the hands and the bezel fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a faint ink mark on the side of one finger. About 80° field of view, deep focus from the hands to the window, no background blur. Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. The sticky notes are completely blank. Exactly one person visible, seen only as two hands and forearms; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere, including the dark monitor screen and the window glass. Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

Seedance 2.5 prompt · 6,749 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the switched-off monitor, the two sticky notes already on its bezel, the third note under the fingers and the position of both hands in frame one; frame one matches this exactly; do not copy any text.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast morning someone at an ordinary office desk presses a third blank sticky note onto the bezel of a switched-off monitor and takes their hands away; a moment later the yellow note beside it lets go and drops.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone held by a colleague crouching just left of the desk, level with the bezel, 35 centimetres from the monitor's lower-left corner, angled slightly up at it. Foreground: fine dust drifting in the window light between the lens and the monitor. Midground: the monitor's lower bezel running across the middle of the frame from the left edge; on it, a pale yellow note on the left, an orange note beside it, and the third orange note under the fingers 3 centimetres to their right; the top edge of a dark keyboard below the bezel; both hands entering from the bottom edge. Background: the switched-off screen above the bezel, a matte charcoal surface with a dull sheen; at the upper-left, a pale grey wall and the edge of a large window with rain on the glass. A pale strip of old sticky residue on the bezel; a white cable running off the right edge of the frame; a plain grey monitor stand. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the bezel, the two notes already stuck to it and both hands; no empty establishing frame.
Only one person's bare hands and forearms are in frame, close, entering from the bottom edge: the cuffs of plain dark everyday sleeves at the wrists, no logos or printed text, five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. The fingertips press and flatten slightly on whatever they touch.
The right hand's index and middle fingers press the third orange note onto the bezel; the left hand holds the small pad of notes low at the bottom-left, closer to the lens, its forearm resting on the edge of the desk. Neither hand touches the screen.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held level with the bezel, 35 centimetres from it. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Handheld by a colleague crouching still: slight micro-shake and the small rise and fall of their breathing, never gimbal-smooth.
Autofocus hunts once, briefly, as the hands pull away at second 2, then locks on the notes.
Exposure holds on the bezel and the hands; the window at the upper-left stays slightly overexposed.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The right fingertips rest on the third note, pressing lightly. End state: fingers on the note.
1-2s: The right thumb runs once along the note's sticky strip from left to right, pressing it flat against the bezel; the paper flexes and settles. End state: three notes in a row on the bezel, the thumb at the right end of the strip.
2-3s: Both hands draw back and down, out of the bottom edge of the frame; the autofocus hunts briefly and locks. End state: the bezel and the three notes alone in frame.
3-4s: At second 3 the pale yellow note on the left curls up from its lower edge, peels away from the bezel and drops, tipping edge-first and swinging once on the air before it falls out of the bottom of the frame onto the keyboard. End state: two orange notes on the bezel and a pale strip of residue where the yellow one was, camera steady.

PHYSICS
The notes are thin paper with a sticky strip only along their top edge: their lower halves lift slightly off the bezel and tremble in the faint draught from the window; the paper creases faintly under the thumb; the falling note is light, swings once and lands without bouncing; the monitor and its stand do not move; the dust keeps drifting slowly in the window light.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the hands and the bezel fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The switched-off screen gives off no light.

The screen gives off almost no light. The screen and keyboard fill about the upper-left half of the frame. Two bare hands enter from the bottom edge of the frame: the left hand holds a small stack of blank white index cards low at the bottom-left, thumb on top; the right hand holds one blank card by its edges 2 centimetres above the desk, about to lay it to the right of the card in the third row. The cuff of a plain mid-blue overshirt at each wrist, no logos or printed text; five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible; the head and face out of frame. Seedance 2.5 prompt · 7,269 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the laptop with its green screen and four corner dots, the cards already laid, the mug and the hands' positions in frame one; frame one matches this exactly; do not copy any text.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast morning someone sits at an ordinary office desk laying blank index cards out like a family tree beside an open laptop, the first sketch of a website's structure, while a colleague films from above their shoulder.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone held still by a colleague standing behind the chair, 60 centimetres above the desk, pointing steeply down over the right shoulder of the person sitting there. Foreground: a thin thread of steam rising towards the lens from the orange enamel mug at the right edge, half cut by the frame. Midground: on the worn wood-effect desk in the right half and lower part of the frame, the cards: one at the top level with the laptop's hinge, two in a row below it, and one in a third row under the left card of the second row; both hands entering from the bottom edge. Background: in the upper-left, the open laptop, its lid tilted back so the green screen faces up towards the lens. A ballpoint pen rolled against the laptop's side; a pale coffee-ring stain near the cards; a white charging cable from the laptop's left side over the desk edge. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the laptop with its green screen, all four corner dots visible, the four cards already laid and both hands; no empty establishing frame.
Only one person's bare hands and forearms are in frame, close, entering from the bottom edge: the cuff of a plain mid-blue overshirt at each wrist, no logos or printed text, five fingers on each hand, knuckle creases and veins visible. The shoulders and face stay out of frame. The fingertips press and flatten slightly on whatever they touch, and the left forearm takes its weight on the edge of the desk.
The left hand holds a small stack of blank cards low at the bottom-left, thumb on top; the right hand holds one blank card by its edges 2 centimetres above the desk, to the right of the card in the third row. Neither hand ever touches the laptop or crosses the screen.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held 60 centimetres above the desk and pointing steeply down. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Held still above the desk by a colleague standing behind the chair: near-static, with slight micro-shake and the small rise and fall of their breathing, never gimbal-smooth.
Camera static while the screen is in frame: no pan, no tilt, no zoom.
Exposure holds on the white cards and the green screen; the cards stay bright but keep their paper texture.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The right hand holds the card just above the desk. End state: card hovering.
1-2s: At second 1 the right hand lays the card flat on the desk, 3 centimetres to the right of the card in the third row, with a soft tap; the fingers slide off it. End state: two cards in the third row.
2-3s: The right thumb pushes the next card off the stack in the left hand and the right fingers take it by its edges. End state: one card in the right hand, the stack one card thinner.
3-4s: The right hand lays it flat at the right end of the third row, 5 centimetres to the right of the second card, a wider gap than the others, with a soft tap. End state: three cards in the third row, the new one set a little too far out.
4-5s: The right index finger slides the new card 2 centimetres sideways to the left to even the gap; it drags slightly on the wood and stops, and the hand comes to rest on the desk edge. End state: three cards evenly spaced in the third row, both hands resting at the bottom edge of the frame, the left hand still holding the stack.
5-6s: Hold; steam drifts from the mug; ambience only. End state: unchanged frame.

PHYSICS
The cards are thin card stock: each one flexes slightly as it is lifted by its edges and lands flat with a soft tap, casting a small soft shadow to the right; the sliding card drags with friction on the wood and stops without drifting on; the fingertips flatten against the cards; the cuffs fold and drag a moment behind the wrists; the steam rises, breaks up and drifts right; the laptop never moves.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the hands and the cards fall a stop darker with soft shadow; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The laptop screen gives off almost no light.
Real skin texture with visible pores and fine hairs on the backs of the hands; a slightly chipped nail on one thumb.
The cuff of a plain mid-blue overshirt; no logos, no printed text. The person is only partly in frame, and their face is never seen.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: small office room tone, rain pattering on the window to the left, a radiator ticking, a kettle rumbling faintly in another room.
Foley: a soft tap as the card lands at 1 second; the dry slip of a card pushed off the stack at 2 seconds; a tap at 3 seconds; the short hiss of the card sliding on the wood at 4 seconds.
No dialogue. The incidental person does not speak; no voices, near or distant.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close room tone, faint handling noise, the rain thin and distant.
No background music. No subtitles. The clip opens on 1 second of ambience only.

FINAL FRAME
The tree of blank cards, one, two and three, beside the laptop's flat green screen with all four corner dots sharp, both hands resting at the bottom edge, steam at the right edge, camera still.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The laptop screen shows a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill from edge to edge, evenly lit, with no interface, no text, no reflections and no glare; all four corners and the bezel stay visible, with one small dark dot in each corner of the green. The screen gives off almost no light.
The index cards are plain white and completely blank on both sides; the laptop has no logo and no stickers; the orange enamel mug is plain, with no print.
Exactly one person visible, seen only as two hands and forearms; no face and no reflection of a face anywhere. No extra people.

Sound, captions, labels, loudness, finishing

  • Native sound stays and carries the film: squeaks, paper, card taps, the murmur and laugh, the kettle click, rain and room tone. Use 4-frame crossfades at every cut so the rain never jumps. Add soft ticks only on the underlines (and one per grid).
  • Music: none by default, because the foley is the rhythm. If you want a bed, use one sparse licensed track (no vocals, no trending or copyrighted audio), at least 20 LU under the foley so the squeaks stay on top, out by 19.4.
  • Captions: there are no spoken words, so there are no word captions. The text cards carry the story. If a platform needs captions, the only entries are [marker squeaks], [indistinct murmur], [laughs] and [kettle clicks off].
  • Disclosure: labels small, lower-left, on throughout (as above). Platform toggles on every post: TikTok AIGC, YouTube altered or synthetic content, Meta AI info. You and your adviser sign off the wording.
  • 9:16 safe zones: all text between 12% and 80% of the height (y 230–1536 of 1920), with 60 px side margins.
  • Loudness: −14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP.
  • Screen key (O-03):
    • corner-pin on the four dots;
    • insert at about 85% white with a slight cool cast;
    • a soft glare pass from the window side (left);
    • a 1–2 px chromatic edge and faint moiré (a phone filming a laptop), plus a grain match;
    • motion matched to the colleague's breathing micro-shake.
  • Finishing: one grain value, one sharpen value and one light grade across all clips (lift the shadows a touch; never teal-and-orange). Upscale once with Higgsfield upscale_video (ugc preset), only if you had to generate at 720p.
  • Never on screen: "No.1", "#1", "first", "now" as a claim, "growth", "+%", up-arrows or count-ups. Also never: Zentro's 5,000+ / 4.8/5 / 2,560+ claims or any of its testimonials; "we built", "Website by" or "our client" for Zentro; any "Ali"; clock or time stamps; Google logos or colours on our graphics.

Rules for the lines:

  • Line 2 is one side of a call only. The client's voice is never heard and never generated.
  • "Morning." stays only if the call really happens in the morning. "In your inbox" stays only if the report really goes by email. Otherwise T2 says what is true, for example "Your report's just gone over."
  • The only number spoken is "twenty-five", said as words, and it must match the receipt (September 2026).
  • Never add: "He'll ring me in about ten minutes", "a hundred and fourteen since May", "best month since May", "number one", "first", "just hit", "up", "more", or any line saying Hulk caused the calls.
  • T2 does not name the client on camera. The receipt names Leam Taxis only with their written OK.

How to record each memo (send this to T2):

  • One line per memo: three takes in the same file, with a 2-second gap between takes.
  • Room: a quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a bedroom or lounge (not the kitchen or a stairwell). No TV, radio or music. Turn any fan off.
  • Phone: about 30 cm from your mouth (production_rules A.3, as in V10 and T2's character file), slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop. Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • Delivery: say it the way you would really say it, not as if reading. Your own accent; nobody ever describes it in a prompt.
  • Then one "real place" take of each line for the final track: line 1 on the front camera at arm's length at the real door (_door); line 2 standing at the real window with your phone at your ear and a second phone recording from the shelf (_room); line 3 at the desk on the front camera at arm's length (_desk).
  • Name the files MEMO_T2_REPORTING_v12_line<n>_t1.m4a, _t2, _t3, plus _door, _room, _desk. We keep the best take as MEMO_T2_REPORTING_v12_line<n>.m4a. Send full size by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.

Which memo goes where: the clean indoor take is @Audio 1 in Seedance, because it guides timbre and pace best. In the edit we lay in the real-place take (_door, _room, _desk) wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like T2, that is a QC fail (production_rules G.1). Never ship a voice T2 hasn't heard and approved.

No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Only the hand, wrist and knit cuff are visible; no face and no reflection of a face in the window or the laptop. Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.
  • Step 2 · Seedance 2.5 prompt:
Seedance 2.5 prompt · 5,465 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: identity of the reporting lead's hands only (skin, knuckles, nails, and the pushed-up cuffs of their navy knit jumper; no logos, no printed text). 100% matches the reference.
@Image 2: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, the hand, the laptop, the lamp and the window in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any screen content or text.
@Image 3: geography and materials of their own desk, lamp and window after dark only; do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, labels or printed text in it.

SCENE CONTEXT
After dark at the end of a wet late-October day, a reporting lead logs off: filming one-handed, their hand closes the laptop and switches off the desk lamp, and the desk drops into blue-grey dusk.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: the reporting lead's own phone held low in their left hand at desk height, about 40 centimetres to the left of the laptop and slightly behind its hinge, looking right across the desk. Foreground left: a plain pale grey mug, empty, with a dried tea ring inside. Midground: the open laptop, side and hinge towards the lens, screen already dark; the right hand on the top edge of the lid; a closed orange notebook with a dark pen across it beside it; a white charging cable trailing off the desk edge. Beyond the laptop: a small desk lamp switched on, its switch on the cable on the desk. Back of frame at screen-left: the window with deep blue-grey dusk and rain beads on the glass.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the right hand on the top edge of the open lid, the laptop, the lit lamp and the mug; no empty establishing frame. Only the back and edge of the lid are visible. No face anywhere.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone main-camera perspective, held low about 40 centimetres from the laptop. Environment visible to the frame edges, deep edge-to-edge focus, no telephoto compression, no creamy bokeh.

CAMERA
Held low in their own left hand: slight handheld micro-shake and one small re-grip, no gimbal smoothness.
Auto exposure breathes when the lamp goes off at second 5, lifting the dark desk and bringing up sensor noise, then settles.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. The hand rests on the top edge of the lid; the lamp lights the desk. End state: still.
1-3s: The hand pushes the lid down; it swings closed and meets the base with a soft clap. End state: the laptop closed, the hand resting on its lid.
3-5s: The hand slides off the laptop, crosses the desk and finds the lamp switch on its cable; at second 5 the thumb presses it and the lamp clicks off. End state: the bulb fading.
5-8s: The bulb fades with a brief orange afterglow; the desk drops into dim blue-grey dusk from the window; the exposure lifts and the shadows fill with sensor noise; the hand withdraws out of frame. End state: the dark desk, the closed laptop, the mug and the notebook in blue-grey dusk, rain on the window.

PHYSICS
The lid has hinge resistance and closes with a soft clap; the base shivers once on the desk. The switch is stiff and clicks. The tungsten bulb does not snap off but fades with an orange afterglow. Rain beads on the window catch less light once the lamp is off.

LIGHTING
The warm tungsten desk lamp beyond the laptop is the only key, throwing a pool of light across the desk towards the lens; cool blue-grey dusk from the window at screen-left beyond the desk; the two colour temperatures meet on the back of the hand and the lid; the corners of the room fall into soft shadow. The warm lamp light falls across the back of the hand, the lid and the desk, and a faint edge of cool window light runs along the lid and the rim of the mug. At second 5 the lamp goes off; after that the only light is the dim blue-grey dusk from the window.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each.

AUDIO
Ambience: a quiet room at night, rain on the dark window, a radiator ticking.
Foley: the lid's soft clap at 2 seconds; fingers sliding on the desk at 3 to 4 seconds; the lamp switch click at 5 seconds.
No dialogue and no voices.
Sound from the phone's microphone: close, quiet room tone, faint handling noise when the grip shifts.
No background music. No subtitles.

FINAL FRAME
The dark desk in blue-grey dusk: the closed laptop, the empty mug in the foreground, the notebook dark in the low light, the dark lamp, rain on the window, the camera almost still.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The laptop screen is angled away from the camera; only the back of the lid is visible.
Only the hand, wrist and knit cuff of one person are visible; no face and no reflection of a face in the window or the laptop. No other people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone main camera: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

    • Screen never seen while the lid closes. Fail → region edit to the back of the lid.

What this video is

  • Concept. A sit-down documentary interview with Hassan at his real desk by a rainy window, deliberately not his black-studio portrait look. He says who Hulk helps, why he started it, what clients actually get every month, and what he will never promise. The human story comes first; the receipts land at 34 s: the Companies House record, then a 6 s montage of three real client receipts on his green laptop.
  • Hook. 16:9: Hassan walking in out of the rain at his real building, shaking and folding an umbrella; his first line lands on the cut to the interview. 9:16: a selfie cold open in drizzle in the car park: "If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, this is why we exist."
  • Why this brand. It is the homepage hero for googlerankerpro.com. It puts a real, named founder in a real room, which the five polished AI service presenters on the site can't do, and it matches the site's own line "No ranking guarantees".
  • What the edit reveals. Hulk Marketing Ltd · company no. 15931335 · incorporated 2 Sep 2024 (Companies House), then Golden Line's 744 different searches, Leam Taxis' 114 calls May–Oct 2026 (October part month) and Coventry's 79 Business Profile interactions May–Oct 2026. Script and voice memos

How the words are made. We send Hassan the four questions. He answers them in one relaxed 10-minute voice memo (MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_interview.m4a), the way he'd talk to a client. We transcribe it and cut it into short lines (drafts below where the plan has them). He edits and approves each line in writing, then records each approved line on its own. Only approved words go into a prompt.

  • Q1 Who do you help, in one sentence?
  • Q2 Why did you start it?
  • Q3 What does a client actually get from you every month?
  • Q4 What will you never promise?
  • Cold open (9:16 only) If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, why do you exist?

Rules for the lines

  • No numbers are spoken. The numbers are ours, on screen as receipts. If his real reason (Q2) includes a number or a year, it must be true and written as words, and we check it before he records.
  • Each line is said in 5–6 s at a natural pace (about 12–14 words). If a line runs longer, shorten the words, not the pace.
  • Never "No.1", "first", "now", "growth", "last quarter", "guaranteed results" or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
  • Clients stay unnamed in the lines. Only "No ranking guarantees" is presented as the site's own line.
  • Q2 is his real reason. We don't write it for him; lines 3 and 4 stay placeholders until he approves his own words.

How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)

  • A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • One line per file: three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, as the file name in the table.
  • Say it the way you'd say it to a client on the phone, not as if reading.
  • Line 8 twice: once indoors as above, and once outdoors in the car park on the phone, held at arm's length (MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v13_line8_outdoor.m4a). The outdoor one is the backup for the selfie's sound and the voice for Version B's 9:16 cold open.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where. Each memo is the @Audio reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC (production_rules G.1). Nothing he hasn't heard and approved is published.

Before pasting any Seedance prompt with a line: replace the quoted words with his approved words exactly, keeping the start second. Lines 2, 3 and 4 are placeholders until then.

Seedance 2.5 prompt · 7,143 characters
ASSET MAP
@Image 1: identity of the agency's founder (face, hair, build, wardrobe: a navy wool suit jacket over an open-collar white shirt, no tie, dark trousers, his own watch; no logos, no printed text). 100% matches the reference.
@Image 2: same man, three-quarter view; identity only.
@Image 3: anchor still for this shot: framing, light direction, wardrobe and room layout in frame one; frame one matches this; do not copy any screen content or text.
@Image 4: geography and materials of his own office room only (window, radiator, desk, chairs, walls); do not copy its camera angle; ignore any screens, signs or printed text in it.
@Audio 1: the founder's own voice for the line at second 1 only; ignore its background noise.
@Audio 2: the founder's own voice for the line at second 8 only; ignore its background noise.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast late-October morning, the founder of a small search agency sits in his own office, just in from the rain, and tells an interviewer who his clients are. It starts settled, turns on a short pause to think, and ends with him holding, his hand drifting to his mug.

LOCATION MAP
Camera on a tripod at seated eye height, 2.5 metres in front of him, facing him and the back wall. The interviewer sits just past camera-left, out of frame. Midground: the founder in a plain grey fabric office chair in the right third of frame; a small low side table at the right edge of frame with an orange enamel mug with a chipped rim on it, steaming. Background, 1.5 metres behind him and softly out of focus: a worn wood-effect desk against a pale grey wall, a plain dark grey laptop closed on it, a charging cable and a power strip drooping under the desk to a floor socket. Left two thirds of frame: a large window at the left edge with rain on the glass and a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked; a radiator with chipped white paint under it; a navy wool overcoat over the back of a second chair beside the radiator; a folded plain dark umbrella leaning against the radiator, a small damp patch on the floor under its tip. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the founder in position; no empty establishing frame. He sits in the right third of frame, about 1.2 metres from the window, framed from just above the head to the top of the thighs. Torso angled slightly towards camera-left; eyes resting just past camera-left on the interviewer; lips closed. Left forearm on the chair's armrest, left hand a few centimetres from the side table; right hand resting loosely on his right knee. The mug stands on the side table, a thin thread of steam rising.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 2 to 3 metres from the subject, natural human-eye perspective, zero obvious distortion, natural face proportions, background readable but softly out of focus.

CAMERA
Locked-off on a tripod with the faint micro-movement of a real head.
Focus stays on the eyes; one small natural focus correction when he shifts in the chair at second 7.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. He sits settled and takes a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak, eyes on the interviewer.
1-7s: At second 1, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "Taxi firms, a fostering agency, local businesses where one phone call matters.", unhurried and plain, his right hand lifting a few centimetres off his knee and opening slightly on "local businesses", then settling back. End state: line finished, lips closed, right hand back on his knee.
7-8s: A short pause: he shifts his weight in the chair and his eyes drop briefly towards the window side to think, then come back to the interviewer. End state: lips parted again.
8-13s: At second 8, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "[APPROVED LINE 2 FROM HIS TRANSCRIPT]", steady, a small lift of the left shoulder on the second half of the line, hands well away from the mouth. End state: line finished, lips closed, one small involuntary nod.
13-15s: He holds, breathing; his left hand slides from the armrest to the side table and his fingers rest on the mug's handle without lifting it; ambience only. End state: fingers on the mug handle, eyes on the interviewer.

PHYSICS
The chair takes his weight and creaks as he shifts at second 7; the suit jacket bunches at the elbow on the armrest and smooths again as he moves; his shirt cuff slides back a little as the hand lifts; when his fingers meet the mug handle the mug nudges a centimetre across the table and the steam bends; the umbrella and the coat stay exactly where they are.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The rain beads on the glass glow in the window light.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each, fingers not touching the face during speech.

AUDIO
Ambience: small office room tone, rain pattering on the window to the left, a radiator ticking, distant traffic on a wet road.
Foley: a fabric rustle as his hand lifts at 4 seconds; a chair creak at 7 seconds; a soft scrape of the mug's enamel base on the table at 14 seconds.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the founder at seconds 1 and 8, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices. The interviewer stays silent.
Clean close dialogue as if from a clip-on microphone, natural room tone underneath, no echo.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The founder seated in the right third of frame, fingers resting on the orange mug's handle, eyes on the interviewer just past camera-left, the rainy window and the coat on the chair soft at the left, camera holding.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The laptop on the desk stays closed.
He blinks naturally, glances away to think, restarts a gesture, adjusts a sleeve, takes a breath before a line, and finishes with a small involuntary nod.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: his own phone's front camera, held in his outstretched right hand 45 centimetres from his face, slightly above eye level. Foreground: the edge of his right forearm and coat sleeve at the lower right. Midground: his head and shoulders, a little off-centre to the left. Background, mostly in focus: a wet tarmac car park with shallow puddles, two plain parked cars standing side-on to the camera, so neither number plate faces the lens, a wet leaf stuck to the bonnet of the nearer car, the side of his office building from @Image 4 at the edge of frame with no sign in view. A few drizzle drops on the lens at the upper left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the founder in position; no empty establishing frame. His head and shoulders sit in the lower two thirds of the vertical frame, a little off-centre to the left, the top of the head at about 38 percent of the frame height, grey sky and his office building above him. Eyes on the lens; lips closed; left hand in his coat pocket; overcoat collar turned up.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone front-camera perspective, lens 40 to 55 cm from the face at arm's length, slightly above eye level. The face sits close and slightly enlarged at the centre, background visible to the frame edges and mostly in focus, straight lines stay straight, no portrait bokeh.

CAMERA
The phone is held in the speaker's own outstretched right hand; the frame moves with their arm: slight handheld micro-shake, small drifts as they gesture with the other hand, a natural re-grip once.
Auto exposure breathes slightly when more of the bright overcast sky comes into frame, then settles.
Their eyes flick between the lens and the screen image of themselves, as people do on a front camera.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. He settles the framing with a small re-grip of the phone and breathes out. End state: eyes on the lens, lips parted, about to speak.
1-8s: At second 1, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "If you run a local business and people can't find you on Google, this is why we exist.", plain, at his natural pace, as if catching it before going in; on "this is why we exist" his left hand comes out of his pocket and his thumb points briefly back over his left shoulder towards the building, below chin height, then drops. End state: line finished, lips closed, left hand down by his side.
8-9s: His eyes flick to the screen image of himself and back to the lens; one small nod. End state: a half-smile, eyes on the lens.
9-10s: His thumb moves towards the screen to stop recording and the frame gives a small jolt; ambience only. End state: the frame tilted slightly, his face still in shot.

PHYSICS
The phone has real weight at arm's length: the frame dips a little after the re-grip and steadies; the overcoat collar stands stiff against his jaw and the wool holds drizzle beads; his breath shows faintly once in the cold air; a drizzle drop on the lens slides a few millimetres down the upper-left corner; the parked cars stay still, settled on their tyres.

LIGHTING
Flat overcast sky as a huge soft source from above; soft shadows under the eyes and chin; wet tarmac reflects the grey sky; no direct sun.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each, fingers not touching the face during speech.

AUDIO
Ambience: drizzle hissing on wet tarmac, a car door closing somewhere across the car park, distant traffic on a wet road.
Foley: a rustle of the coat sleeve with the re-grip at 0 seconds; the coat pocket rustling as his hand comes out at 6 seconds; a faint tap and handling bump on the phone at 9 seconds.
Dialogue: only the quoted line, spoken by the founder at second 1, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices.
Sound recorded by the phone's built-in microphone at arm's length: close voice with a little room reflection, faint handling noise when the grip shifts.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
His face close in the vertical frame, a half-smile, the frame tilted slightly as his thumb reaches to stop recording, the wet car park behind him.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted autumn colour as it really looks: wet slate greys, an overcast white sky, wet black tarmac, red-brick terraces and cream stucco, cold white LED and older amber street light; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The car has real weight: suspension settles after it stops, tyres flex on the kerb, road grime along the sills, rain beads on the bonnet, reflections of the grey sky distort across the panels. Both cars were parked before the shot starts and never move.
The parked cars are plain, with no livery or decals, and stay parked; they stand side-on, so neither number plate faces the lens. He stands still; nobody drives.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people.
Filmed handheld on a smartphone front camera at arm's length: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

What this video is

  • Concept. A weekly 30-second tip from Hassan, filmed on his own phone on a little desk tripod: the same desk, framing and jumper every week, so it reads as a real habit. In the edit we cut him out of his real room with a matte (the "green-screen effect", no physical green screen) and put the real Search Console row behind him in the top third. He points up at it.
  • Hook. A myth line in the first second ("Myth: you need more content to rank. Usually you don't."), with the receipt taxi warwick · 665 times shown · avg 10.7 behind him by 0.8 s.
  • The tip. Find a search with lots of impressions sitting around position ten, then fix the page you already have (title, local proof, links from your other pages) instead of writing a new blog.
  • Why this brand. Golden Line is the one client where the agency credit is verified (live footer "Made with ❤ by Hulk Marketing Ltd"), and its row 5 is a textbook "edge of page one" case: shown 665 times at an average position of 10.7 with a 0.9% click-through. V15 later reports the whole Warwick cluster.
  • What the edit reveals. Golden Line's real row 5 (goldenlinetaxiswarwick_gsc_3m.png, 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026): 6 clicks, 665 impressions, 0.9% CTR, position 10.7, with the source line and "average position" context on screen.

Agency draft. Hassan edits it, approves it in writing, then records each approved line on its own. Numbers are said as words, exactly as written. If he rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.

Where every number comes from: goldenlinetaxiswarwick_gsc_3m.png row 5, crop 24, 1100, 1318, 49: "taxi warwick", 6 clicks, 665 impressions, 0.9% CTR, position 10.7, window 19 Jul–18 Oct 2026 ("three months"). 6 ÷ 665 = 0.9%, so "fewer than one in a hundred" is true.

Rules for the lines

  • Impressions are "times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched".
  • 10.7 is an average position: "averaging ten point seven", "the edge of page one". Never "page one", "No.1", "first", "now", "just hit", "last quarter" or a causal verb (made, drove, caused).
  • Each line is one memo at his natural pace: lines 1 and 2 about 3–4 s, line 3 about 6–7 s, line 4 about 5 s, line 5 about 7 s, line 6 about 2 s. If a line runs long, cut words, not pace.

How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)

  • A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • One line per file: three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, and send it back to you under the file name in the table. Upload only that trimmed one-take file as @Audio, never the raw three-take recording.
  • Say it the way you'd explain it to a client across the desk, not as if reading.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where. Each memo is the @Audio reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC (production_rules G.1). Nothing he hasn't heard and approved is published.

Before pasting any Seedance prompt with a line: replace the quoted words with his approved words exactly, keeping the start second.

Version B (T1): we send T1 the same five lines. T1 edits, approves and records three takes of each line as team.md §7 describes (MEMO_T1_SEO_v14_line<n>_t1.m4a, _t2, _t3); we send back the best takes, trimmed, as MEMO_T1_SEO_v14_line1.m4a to _line5.m4a.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet late-October morning the founder of a small search agency sits at his own desk and records his weekly tip on his phone, which stands on a little tripod in front of him. He starts settled, turns on a point up and over his shoulder as he names the method, and ends back at rest with a small nod.

LOCATION MAP
Camera: a phone on a small plain black tripod standing on the desk, at his chest height, about 65 centimetres from his face, pointing slightly up at him. Foreground: the near edge of the desk across the bottom of frame, his forearms on it; at the lower right edge, half cut off, an orange enamel mug with a chipped rim, steaming; a phone charging cable drooping off the desk edge at the lower left. Midground: the founder in his desk chair, a little right of centre. Background: a plain pale grey wall 2 metres behind him; at screen-right, 1.5 metres behind him, a second chair with a navy wool overcoat over its back. Left edge of frame, 1 metre to his right: a large window with rain on the glass, a plain white roller blind hanging slightly crooked, a small potted plant in a plain grey pot on the sill. Window light from camera-left.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains the founder in position; no empty establishing frame. He sits a little right of centre, the top of his head about one third of the way down the frame, the upper third plain wall and the top of the window. Torso faces the camera; eyes on the lens; lips closed. Both forearms rest on the desk edge, hands loosely together just above the bottom of frame. The mug steams at the lower right edge.

FORMAT MODE
SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

OPTICS
About 80° diagonal field of view, phone front-camera perspective, lens about 65 centimetres from the face, a little below eye level. The face sits near the centre with clear wall above the head, background visible to the frame edges and mostly in focus, straight lines stay straight, no portrait bokeh.

CAMERA
The phone is propped on a small tripod on the desk at chest height, about 65 cm from the face; the frame is static except for faint vibration when the desk is touched.
Framing is a little off-centre to screen-right, the top of his head about one third of the way down the frame, plain wall above him.
His eyes stay mostly on the lens and flick now and then to the screen image of himself, as people do on a front camera.
Auto exposure breathes slightly when his raised arm moves in front of the bright window side, then settles.

TIMELINE
0-1s: Ambience only. He sits settled, forearms on the desk, and takes a small breath in. End state: lips parted, about to speak, eyes on the lens.
1-5s: At second 1, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "Myth: you need more content to rank. Usually you don't.", plain and a little dry, a short pause after "Myth", one small shake of the head on "Usually you don't." His hands stay loosely together on the desk. End state: line finished, lips closed, a faint half-smile.
5-9s: At second 5 his right hand leaves the desk and rises beside his right shoulder until it is level with his ear, about 15 centimetres out from his head and fully inside the frame, and his index finger points up and back over his right shoulder towards the upper screen-left corner of the frame, without his head turning; at the same second, @Image 1 the founder says, in natural British English, "Find a search with loads of impressions sitting around position ten.", steady and practical, eyes on the lens, one flick to the screen image of himself. The hand never passes in front of his face. End state: line finished, the hand still raised, finger pointing.
9-11s: At second 9 the hand drops back to the desk and his forearm lands on the desk edge; he settles. End state: both forearms on the desk, lips closed, eyes on the lens.
11-12s: He holds and gives one small involuntary nod; ambience only. End state: still, eyes on the lens.

PHYSICS
The chair takes his weight and creaks softly as he settles at second 10; as his arm rises the jumper sleeve slides back a few centimetres and the knit folds at the elbow; his forearm lands on the desk with real weight and the desk passes one faint shiver into the tripod, so the frame trembles once; the steam from the mug wavers as the desk shivers; rain runnels slide down the window glass in short jerks.

LIGHTING
Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. The shadow side is his left cheek, at screen-right, away from the window; no lamp in frame. Faint dust drifts in the window light. The phone filming him adds no visible light.
Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched.
Hands relaxed with natural knuckle creases and veins; five fingers each, fingers not touching the face during speech.

AUDIO
Ambience: small office room tone, rain pattering on the window to the left, a radiator ticking, distant traffic on a wet road.
Foley: a soft knit rustle as his arm rises at 5 seconds; a dull thump of his forearm on the desk at 9 seconds; a chair creak at 10 seconds.
Dialogue: only the quoted lines, spoken by the founder at seconds 1 and 5, in natural British English; lips still when not speaking; no other voices.
Sound recorded by the phone's built-in microphone about 65 centimetres away: clear voice with a little room reflection, no handling noise.
No background music. No subtitles. At least 1 second of ambience-only before the first word and after the last word.

FINAL FRAME
The founder a little right of centre, both forearms on the desk, eyes on the lens, lips closed, plain wall above his head, the mug steaming at the lower right edge, the rainy window at the left, camera static.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated.
One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook.
No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable.
The phone that films him is never in frame, and no other screen is visible.
He blinks naturally, glances away to think, restarts a gesture, adjusts a sleeve, takes a breath before a line, and finishes with a small involuntary nod.
Exactly one person visible. No extra people, and no reflection of anyone in the window.
Filmed on a smartphone front camera propped in a mount at chest height: small-sensor look with deep focus, slight edge over-sharpening, faint sensor noise in the shadows, auto exposure and auto white balance as recorded, ungraded colour.

Rules for the lines

  • Every number matches assets/gsc/gsc_data.json: rows 20, 6, 7 (5.3, 6.1, 7.1), row 4 (6.7), rows 5, 9, 3 (665 + 486 + 371 = 1,522, at 10.7, 12.6, 11.5). If Hassan rewords a line, the numbers stay exactly as they are.
  • Offered for Hassan's approval in line 3: "the three airport searches average page one" (it names exactly the three rows shown). Keep the current wording if he prefers it.
  • "Times shown", never "people saw" or "people searched". "Last three months", never "last quarter".
  • No causal verbs (made, drove, caused), no "No.1", "first", "just hit", "growth". "Here's what Google shows now" is the plan's approved framing, kept as written.
  • Each line is said at a natural pace, the way he'd say it to a client on the phone. If a line runs past its "must end by" second, shorten the words, not the pace.

How to record a memo (send this to Hassan)

  • A quiet room with soft furnishings, such as a lounge or bedroom (not a kitchen or stairwell). No TV, radio, fan or music.
  • Hold the phone about 30 cm from your mouth, slightly to one side so your breath doesn't pop.
  • Voice Memos on its lossless setting (or any 44.1 or 48 kHz recorder), mono. Peaks around −6 to −3 dBFS. If a take sounds distorted, record it again.
  • One line per file: three takes in the same file with a 2-second gap between them. We keep the best take, trimmed to the line plus 0.3 s, under the file name in the table.
  • Send us Hassan's raw memo; we send back MEMO_F1_HASSAN_v15_lineN.m4a (one take, line + 0.3 s). Attach only that file as @Audio, never the raw three-take file.
  • Send full-size files by AirDrop, Google Drive or email. Not WhatsApp.
  • His accent is never described in any prompt. The memo carries the voice.

Which memo goes where. Each memo is the @Audio reference in its Seedance shot (it guides timbre and pace), and we lay the real memo in as the final track wherever sync allows. If the generated voice doesn't sound like Hassan, the clip fails QC (production_rules G.1). Before pasting any Seedance prompt: replace the quoted words with his approved words exactly, keeping the start second.

A single frame of documentary video filmed handheld on a wet, overcast late-October afternoon: the man in the attached reference images, 100% matching his face, hair, build and proportions, stands beside a wall monitor in his own small office from the attached room photo, about to explain something to an interviewer. The camera is at standing eye height about 3 metres from him, a little towards the window side, about 47° field of view, framing him from mid-thigh to a little above his head: natural perspective, the wall and monitor just behind him only a touch softer than his face. He stands just left of centre, about 30 centimetres in front of the pale grey wall and 40 centimetres to the left of the monitor's left edge, his body three-quarter towards the camera, his head turned to his left towards the monitor. His left arm is raised with a plain dark grey pen held between thumb and two fingers, pointing at the upper third of the screen, the pen tip about 15 centimetres in front of the glass; his right hand hangs loose at his side. The wall monitor fills most of the right half of the frame, seen at a slight angle: a plain dark flat screen about 1.2 metres wide with nothing printed on its bezel, its bottom edge about 1.2 metres above the floor. The screen shows a flat, uniform, matte chroma-green fill from edge to edge, evenly lit, with no interface, no text, no reflections and no glare; all four corners and the bezel stay visible, with one small dark dot in each corner of the green. The screen gives off almost no light. His hand and the pen overlap only the left part of the green and never cover a corner dot. The monitor's power cable hangs loose down the wall below it in a slight kink to a floor socket. Wearing a navy wool suit jacket over an open-collar white shirt, no tie, dark trousers, his own watch; no logos, no printed text; the jacket creased at the elbows, one side of the shirt collar sitting a little flatter than the other. At the left edge of the frame: the window with rain beads and short runnels on the glass, a plain white roller blind pulled a third of the way down and hanging slightly crooked, a radiator with chipped white paint under it, a navy wool overcoat over the back of a chair beside the radiator. Behind him on the left, a touch soft: a worn wood-effect desk against the wall with a plain dark grey laptop closed on it, a switched-off desktop monitor, and an orange enamel mug with a small chip on the rim, plain, no print, a thin thread of steam rising from it. If a room photo is attached, take only the room, the wall, the monitor's position, the furniture and the materials from it, and ignore any text, labels or screen content in it; if a mug photo is attached, take only the orange mug's shape, colour and chip. Soft overcast daylight from a large window camera-left is the only key; the right side of the face falls a stop darker with soft shadow under the cheekbone; the overhead office lights are on but weak, adding a faint cooler top light; the window itself is slightly overexposed. With his head turned towards the monitor, more of his face sits on the shadow side. Natural skin from the references, visible pores and fine texture, unretouched. Muted, lived-in indoor colour as it really looks: off-white and pale grey walls, worn wood and grey laminate, cool daylight at the window, a warm pocket of light from a lamp or ceiling bulb; people in navy, grey and mid-blue everyday clothes; nothing saturated. One small warm orange object in frame, such as a mug or a notebook. No on-screen text, captions or subtitles. All signs, labels, mugs, clothing, papers and screens are plain or turned away, with no readable words, logos or numbers. Number plates are not readable. Exactly one person visible, and no reflection of anyone in the window or the monitor bezel. Filmed on a handheld documentary video camera in available light: natural colour with a restrained grade, fine even digital grain, soft highlight roll-off on bright windows, real depth of field with a gently soft background.

SCENE CONTEXT
On a wet, overcast late-October afternoon, the founder of a small search agency stands at a wall monitor in his own office and starts explaining a client's results to an interviewer.   • Sound: Seedance's native room tone and foley stay; his real memos are laid in wherever sync allows, checked frame by frame. No music under A-01. One optional sparse licensed bed under −20 LU from 13 s to the end; a soft tick on each underline; no trending or copyrighted audio.

  • Finishing: one grain value, one sharpen value for all of V15; a light grade (lift the shadows a touch, no teal-and-orange). If clips came back at 720p: Higgsfield upscale_video, aigc preset, once, on every V15 clip.
